compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: https://trust.moveworkforward.com/
https://trust.moveworkforward.com/
Our app doesn't do any redirects / forwards.
Our app doesn't rely on URL for its features.
Our app is frontend only (no backend), so we don't store any logs.

We don't have access to customer data. However, our monday.com instance responsible for managing the application require employees to use our SSO combined with a Two-Factor Authentication. Also, only our administrators can reach the app administration.
Customer data is stored in the monday.com internal storage. This storage is only accessible by logged users on the customer monday.com instance. So no one in our company can access customer data.
Sanitization is performed on data inputted by users by our framework (React) and raw data are never displayed "as-is". Also, inputted URL are verified to avoid embedding malicious websites.
Our app isn't subject to CSRF attack since we don't have backend or actions executed through URL.
In case of security breach, we have several point of contact (email, Slack, private community) to inform monday.com and solve the issue.
We regularly run dependencies scans to track vulnerabilities and patch them when detected.

Customer data is stored in the monday.com internal storage. As stated in the monday.com documentation, this storage "is compartmentalized according to the accountId and app, so data from one [customer] account is not accessible from others."

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: https://trust.moveworkforward.com/
https://trust.moveworkforward.com/
Our app doesn't do any redirects / forwards.
Our app doesn't rely on URL for its features.
Our app is frontend only (no backend), so we don't store any logs.

We don't have access to customer data. However, our monday.com instance responsible for managing the application require employees to use our SSO combined with a Two-Factor Authentication. Also, only our administrators can reach the app administration.
Customer data is stored in the monday.com internal storage. This storage is only accessible by logged users on the customer monday.com instance. So no one in our company can access customer data.
Sanitization is performed on data inputted by users by our framework (React) and raw data are never displayed "as-is". Also, inputted URL are verified to avoid embedding malicious websites.
Our app isn't subject to CSRF attack since we don't have backend or actions executed through URL.
In case of security breach, we have several point of contact (email, Slack, private community) to inform monday.com and solve the issue.
We regularly run dependencies scans to track vulnerabilities and patch them when detected.

Customer data is stored in the monday.com internal storage. As stated in the monday.com documentation, this storage "is compartmentalized according to the accountId and app, so data from one [customer] account is not accessible from others."

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: Our app support, which forwards all security or privacy related question to the correct person. Reachable under app-support@decadis.de or https://support.decadis.net/
We are currently in the process of getting ISO 27001 certified.
As a company based in Europe, we are legally required to comply with GDPR.
This does not apply to our app as there is no possibility to enter links that forward or redirect outside monday.
We only take input via monday components and don't have any own api or backend which could be targeted by a mass parameter assignment attacks.
We are not pertaining any logs, so no secrets or PII can be stored accidentally.
All employees with customer data access are required to use 2-Factor-Authentication to login and access the data.

We transfer and store customer PII during the life-cycle events of the app 
(during licensing via the marketplace) for contractual communication.
As such, a group of privileged users has access to this data, to be able to support our customers on contractual matters.
Details about which data is stored and retention periods can be found in our Data Security & Privacy Statement: https://apps.decadis.net/display/DECADIS/Data+Security+and+Privacy+Statement
We only use React components provided by monday, which means all input is sanitized by the React framework. In addition, we don't use any dangerouslySetInnerHTML-function that could circumvent it.
As our app is frontend-only using only components provided by monday.com, there are neither targets nor means for an CSRF-attack

In case of a critical or high severity incident (actively exploited or very high vulnerability) affecting our monday apps or monday customer data, we will immediately inform monday via the developer support contact form.

There is no separate service requiring application-level updates. Our app runs entirely within monday, so all required updates there are done automatically by monday.
For vulnerabilities in our code or included software packages, we provide security patches within 90 days of the vulnerability becoming known.

Each customers configuration data is only stored in their instance itself. This segregates their data by design.
We also store some app sales life-cycle events for contractual communication, which are also logically segregated in data storage.

The newly launched monday.com app for Canva allows users to seamlessly integrate Canva and monday.com to collaborate, manage your team’s workload, track projects, and move work forward on the Canva platform.


Features

The Monday.com app for Canva simplifies the way users work in Canva. It optimizes their workflows by reducing tab/context switching. Once authenticated, a user can perform all the following monday.com tasks from the object panel within Canva.

  • View workspaces, boards, files and items that a user has access to

How to get started

To use the monday.com app in Canva, users must first ensure the app has been installed on their monday.com workspace by a workspace admin. Admins can do so by accessing the app listing here. Once this has been done all users of the workspace will be able to access the monday.com app in Canva by locating the listing in Canva’s app marketplace and following the prompts to authenticate.


For further instructions on how to use the app in Canva, please check out this support guide.

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: Empyra is ISO certified company
The app does not send any data outside of monday.com

The app stores log data securely on our server. Access to these logs is restricted to authorized personnel and is used solely for monitoring, debugging, and ensuring the proper functioning of the application.

The app stores all application data securely on our server. Access is restricted to authorized personnel, and the data is protected using appropriate security measures to ensure confidentiality and integrity.
Yes, we have a dedicated security and privacy point of contact for such issues or questions.
Yes, the app does not forward to any unapproved destinations.

Yes, the app protects against mass parameter assignment attacks. Only explicitly allowed fields are bound to data models or database operations. Input is whitelisted or validated server-side, and sensitive fields such as roles, permissions, and internal IDs are never exposed to the client or modifiable via user input.

Yes, the developer ensures that application logs do not contain secrets or personally identifiable information (PII). All console and log statements are reviewed before deployment to confirm that no confidential or sensitive data is included in the logs.

Yes, we enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all employee access to systems that may process customer data. MFA is enabled for signing in to our servers, ensuring that access requires both a password and a second authentication factor to enhance security.

Yes, access to customer data is protected based on the principle of least privilege. Employees and services are granted only the minimum level of access necessary to perform their specific roles. Access controls are reviewed periodically to ensure that permissions remain appropriate and unnecessary access is promptly removed.

Yes, the app performs input sanitization and output encoding to protect against Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks. We ensure that any user-supplied input is validated and sanitized before processing or storing, and HTML encoding is applied when displaying user data in the frontend. We also use secure libraries/frameworks that automatically escape outputs in templates and prevent script injection.

Yes, all state-changing actions are protected against Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF). The app implements CSRF tokens for all forms and API endpoints that modify state. These tokens are validated server-side, and only requests with valid, trusted tokens are processed.
Yes, we have a mechanism to notify monday.com in the event of a security breach.

Yes, the developer follows a defined process for regularly applying application-level updates and security patches. This includes:

Monitoring official sources (e.g., package managers, vendor advisories) for updates.

Periodically updating software packages, libraries, and dependencies.

Applying database security patches in coordination with the infrastructure team.

Using automated tools (e.g., Dependabot, npm audit, pip-audit, etc.) to detect vulnerabilities.

Testing updates in a staging environment before deployment to production.

Yes, customer data is logically segregated from the data of other customers. This is achieved through the use of unique identifiers (IDs) for each customer, ensuring that their data is kept separate and secure.

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: Although customer data shares the same database schema, we ensure data isolation through stringent logical segregation. Each customer is assigned a unique identifier used in all database requests, ensuring access only to their own data. Robust access controls, authentication mechanisms, and regular security audits are in place to maintain the integrity and effectiveness of our data segregation measures.

We approach application level updates and security patched with the following steps:

a) Monitor: Keep an eye out for any updates or security patches for your software.
   
b) Evaluate: Decide if the updates are necessary and plan when to install them.
   
c)  Backup: Make a copy of your data and settings before updating.
   
d) Test: Try the updates in a test environment to make sure they work properly.
   
e) Deploy: Install the updates in the real (production) environment.

In case of a security breach we would do the following:

a) Assessment: Immediately assess the nature, scope, and potential impact of the breach.
b) Notification: Notify monday.com within 24 hours of discovering the breach via email or phone call, providing all available details of the breach, including its nature, the data affected, potential consequences, and measures taken to address it.
c) Updates: Provide continuous updates as more information becomes available and as additional steps are taken to address the breach.
d) Compliance: Ensure compliance with all legal and regulatory requirements for data breach notification.

To protect all state-changing actions against CSRF (Cross-Site Request Forgery), we implement a combination of measures depending on relevancy for the app.  Most of this is done by the frameworks we use and include the following:

a) Use of Anti-CSRF Tokens: We generate unique tokens for each session and include them in forms and AJAX requests. The server verifies the token before processing any state-changing request.

b) Same-Site Cookies: We set the 'SameSite' attribute for cookies to 'Strict' or 'Lax' to ensure the browser only sends the cookie in a first-party context.

c) Checking the Origin and Referer Headers: We validate the origin and referer headers of the HTTP request to ensure it came from a trusted domain.

d) Requiring Authentication: For any state-changing action, we require the user to be authenticated and authorized.

e) Implementing Security Headers: We implement HTTP security headers like Content-Security-Policy (CSP) to control the sources from which content can be loaded.

To prevent XSS (Cross-Site Scripting) attacks, we implement the following measures for encoding and sanitizing all user-supplied parameters where relevant:

a) Input Validation: We validate all user input to ensure it conforms to expected formats and does not contain any malicious code or characters.

b) Output Encoding: We encode all user-supplied data before rendering it in the HTML output. This ensures that any potentially malicious code inserted by the user is treated as plain text and not executable script.

c)  Use of Content-Security-Policy (CSP) Header: We implement CSP headers to restrict the sources from which content can be loaded and executed by the browser.

d)  Use of Sanitization Libraries: We use established libraries and frameworks that have built-in sanitization features to automatically sanitize user input and protect against XSS attacks.

Access to customer data at our company is limited to:

a) Customer Support: Limited access for resolving customer issues.
b) Operations and IT: Access for maintaining and managing infrastructure.
c)  Management: Access to aggregated and anonymized data for strategic decisions.

Access is based on the principle of least privilege.

Our employees use Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for accessing systems that process or hold customer data, which is hosted on AWS. AWS MFA involves the use of two different factors for authentication: something you know (your AWS account password) and something you have (an authentication device). This ensures that even if one's password is compromised, an attacker would still need access to the authentication device to gain access to the AWS resources.

We ensure logs do not contain secrets or personally identifiable information (PII) by:


a) Log Sanitization: Before logs are written, we sanitize the data to remove any sensitive information by filtering out known sensitive fields and replacing them with placeholder values.


b) Use of Logging Libraries: We use logging libraries and frameworks designed to automatically mask or remove sensitive information from logs.


c)  Regular Audits: Logs are regularly audited to ensure that no sensitive data has inadvertently been logged. Automated tools help in scanning through large volumes of logs to identify any potential leaks.


d) Employee Training: Employees are trained to recognize sensitive data and to avoid logging such information inadvertently. They are also trained on how to use the logging libraries and frameworks correctly to ensure sensitive data is automatically removed or masked.

Our monday.com app safeguards against mass parameter assignment attacks by:

a) Whitelisting Parameters: Only allowing modifications to predefined and whitelisted parameters.
b) Strong Parameter Validation: Ensuring data received is of expected type, format, and range.
c) Authentication and Authorization: Requiring users to authenticate and checking their permissions before processing user data.
d) Object-Level Security: Ensuring users can only modify authorized objects within their monday.com workspace.

These combined measures ensure robust protection against mass parameter assignment attacks.

Our app only allows redirects to a select few destinations and does not permit users to determine or add a redirect destination. Additionally, we verify user input data before authorizing any operations, such as forwards or redirects, and we validate the URLs/destinations, permitting only those on the approved list.

This powerful traceability app allows you to track your links endlessly, providing a comprehensive understanding of the linked items within your workflow.


Book your Demo


Key Benefits


  • ✅End-to-End Traceability: This project management tool ensures that every link within your project is meticulously tracked, offering a clear and comprehensive tree view of the entire traceability landscape.


  • ✅Unlimited Tracking: Unlike monday.com, which visualizes links at one level at a time, our impact analysis app takes a revolutionary approach to trace links without limitations.   • ✅Enhanced Visibility: Elevate your trace links with Links Explorer, delving into the interconnected links for an in-depth impact analysis that goes beyond the surface, providing a comprehensive understanding of your project's dynamics.



Additional Benefits


Links Explorer presents a tree view of linked items beyond conventional tracking methods. The visual representation of this monday planning tool enhances your ability to comprehend and manage complex link structures.

Links Explorer's tree view seamlessly integrates with monday, offering customizable tree nodes that empower users to prioritize and focus on the specific information that matters to them, enhancing workflow efficiency.


How to Get Started?

For those eager to explore the capabilities of our app, detailed documentation is readily available. Discover more about the project management app, its features, and how it can transform your project by visiting our blogs.


Elevate your project management experience with Links Explorer on monday!

Publish and share boards online in minutes.


Perfect for showcasing your product or service catalogue, a directory, online booking site, and anything else you store in boards.

Board Publisher is the best way to publicly share monday.com boards through a clean, highly customisable experience. With detailed configuration and display options, customise how your published boards look with ease, in minutes.

Have a question or want more information? Click here to visit our help guides or to contact us. Book a demo with us here or see an example of Board Publisher in action here.


⚙️ Dynamic filtering & categorisation

Use our configuration options to categorise your content into collections and add dynamic filters based on the columns you select.


🖥️ Table and grid views

Customise the appearance of your published boards with multiple board views, allowing you to set defaults or choose which ones to show.


🔥 Get creative with formulas

We support the formula column, allowing for truly dynamic data and messaging to show on your board based on other columns values.


💡 Claim your own subdomain or add your own custom domain

Have all your boards published on the same domain with different slugs for consistent branding and easy-to-find boards.


🚀 Item detail page

Each item comes with its own dedicated page, in addition to the "all items" page, allowing you to provide more details on each item and directly link to specific items.


Highlights:

  • Fine-grained control over each column, allowing for customisation such as show and hide conditions, appearance customisations, and more.
  • Create buttons from column values to link to external pages (such as product checkout links, more information etc).
  • Add standalone elements to the item detail page to make certain values stand out (such as a description or product notice).
  • Use monday.com formulas to show calculated data on the board.
  • No coding required, easy to setup.
  • Published securely with HTTPS and SSL encryption.

marketplace_apps.description:
🏆 Best selling app on monday.com for 2 years in a row 🏆


In short:


✅ Add the same item to multiple boards, including subitems, updates and columns

✅ Replace connected boards & mirror columns with regular, fully functional columns

✅ Post updates from any board and maintain a single, unified update thread across all boards

✅ SOC2 & HIPAA compliant — enterprise-grade security you can trust

✅ 100% native to monday's platform


If you’re using monday.com, you’ve probably run into this:

You want the same item to appear in multiple boards — maybe one for each team, project, or client — but... 😵

You end up duplicating the item, mirroring columns, setting up messy automations, or losing data altogether.

Same Item Multiple Boards is your elegant fix. It lets you share and sync a single item across multiple boards, so updates, columns, subitems — even replies — stay perfectly in sync.


Features


💥 One item. Multiple boards - Create items that live on multiple boards.

💥 Sync updates & subitems - Comments, updates, and even subitems are reflected across all shared boards in real time.

💥 Choose what to share. Only want to sync certain columns? Avoid subitems syncing? You’re in control.

💥 Post updates from anywhere. Keep conversations centralized even when team members are on different boards.

💥 Automations & workflows. Set up cross-board automations, connect items to subitems, and build scalable systems without breaking a sweat.

💥 Build master boards. Aggregate tasks from different boards into one clean overview board — no custom automation gymnastics required.


Who it’s for


  • Agencies juggling multiple client boards
  • Teams managing the same work across departments
  • Project managers building cross-board workflows
  • Businesses in healthcare or other regulated industries
  • Anyone who wants to automate smarter and work cleaner


Got Questions? We’ve Got You Covered


📅 Book a Demo Call (Same-Day Availability!)

💬 Start a Chat!

📖 Read Tutorials


Install it now and feel the difference!

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: The app is not currently certified under ISO/IEC 27001:2022. However, it is secured in compliance with SOC 2 Type II, which provides independent assurance that our system’s security controls are effectively designed and operating as intended to protect customer data.

Yes, the app sends data outside of monday.com to operate the sync functionality. This includes both customer-submitted data (like item names and column values selected for sync) and non-customer-submitted data (like board IDs, item IDs, and user IDs for audit/logging purposes).

All data sent is necessary for providing the sync service and is encrypted in transit and at rest.

The app stores logs in DigitalOcean’s infrastructure, where the production environment is hosted. Logs include actions made to cloud resources and storage, and they are retained for the life of the account. Logs are encrypted at rest.

The app data is stored in DigitalOcean’s infrastructure, which provides secure and scalable storage. Customer data is encrypted at rest and in transit, and DigitalOcean’s global data centers are used, with data location depending on the deployment region.
Yes, the developer performs an annual external web application penetration test. High and critical issues are addressed promptly, and re-tests are done as needed.
Yes, the developer has a Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) responsible for security and privacy matters.

While we are not certified under GDPR-specific standards, our compliance with SOC 2 Type II ensures that strong security controls are in place to protect personal data. We also implement data protection practices aligned with GDPR principles, including data encryption, access controls, and support for data subject rights.
The app does not redirect or forwards to outside destinations
Yes, the developer enforces multi-factor authentication (MFA) for accessing systems that process customer data, including production environments and sensitive tools.
Yes, access to customer data is restricted based on the principle of least privilege, using a role-based access control matrix and quarterly reviews of permissions.
penetration testing and vulnerability scanning are conducted.

Secure HTTP Headers: We use the helmet middleware to set secure HTTP headers, such as X-Frame-Options and Content Security Policy (CSP), which help prevent related vulnerabilities like clickjacking and cross-site scripting (XSS).
Yes, the developer has an Incident Response Policy with procedures to notify customers and legal authorities, which would include notifying monday.com.

Yes, the developer follows a formal Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) with a process for application updates, including mandatory testing, change management, and vulnerability scanning. Security patches are applied as needed.
Yes, customer data is segregated through encrypted identifiers to ensure that only authorized users can access their specific data, enforcing logical segregation

Introducing Docs Builder, a powerful integration designed to revolutionize document creation within monday.com. Bid farewell to manual processes and embrace an efficient workflow with Docs Builder.

Generate PDF documents seamlessly from Google Docs templates, replacing placeholders with real-time data from your monday.com boards. This automated approach ensures precision and consistency in every document.


Key Features:

  • Effortless Integration: Find "Docs Builder" in the monday.com Marketplace, install it, select your target board, and follow the prompts for setup.
  • Template Preparation: Create a Google Docs template with designated placeholders (e.g., {{CustomerName}}, {{InvoiceNumber}}) and save it in Google Drive.
  • Create a Recipe: Customize a recipe to your needs, choosing where to save the generated PDFs.
  • Generating PDF Files: When you run your recipe, Docs Builder automatically starts the document generation process.
  • Output File Placement: PDFs are saved based on your column selection during recipe creation.


Use Case Example:

Imagine you run a small business and need to create invoices for your clients. With Docs Builder, this process is a breeze.


Set up a Google Docs template with placeholders like {{CustomerName}}, {{InvoiceNumber}}, and {{AmountDue}}. In your monday.com board, you have an item with details like Name: John Doe, Invoice: INV-001, Amount: $1000.


With Docs Builder, these details are seamlessly integrated into your template, resulting in a complete, professional invoice ready for saving and sending.

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: Once in a year
security@appfire.com

HIPAA requirements do not normally apply to Appfire and its products, since we do not store or process protected health information (PHI).  As such, a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) is not required.
https://trust.appfire.com/?itemName=certifications&source=click
https://trust.appfire.com/?itemUid=45220873-6e51-4dbb-b1b1-37d66ee9ef95&source=click

The application is only opening links to monday.com and Appfire resources. In our application, it's not possible for the user to save any data with links that later could be displayed for users to click.

We are using @sinclair/typebox in our backend to check all request input data. There are different type schemas with validation for each endpoint. Additionally, we also do not use the input data directly, we always assign it to another object before using it.
All code changes requires at least one team member to review it. It's part of the review process to make sure that no secrets neither PII will be logged.
Only a few people have access to the database, and the access is only permitted for support and optimization purposes.

We use Middy security middleware in which provides XSS encoding and sanitization. See https://middy.js.org/docs/middlewares/http-security-headers/. Additionally, the user-supplied parameters we receive are only numeric. They are properly validated in the backend and would not allow HTML injection. We also rely on the React.js library in which has built-in sanitization methods enabled by default.

All requests to our backend api requires a security header with a token generated by the monday SDK, obtained inside of the monday.com app iframe. There's no authentication or session data on the client side linked to our api URL. XSS attack could facilitate the CSRF attack, but our application is protected against XSS attack. So this also eliminates the possibility of using XSS to bypass both referrer and token security checks.

Appfire Infosec to be notified of a security incident through internal ticketing system and Slack. Infosec will analyze the issue and notify monday.com within 24 hours. It is part of our incident handling ISO process.

Application-level updates are done by the team, we analyze all dependencies with Snyk and handle critical and high severity updates immediately. Other updates are planned by the team and done on regular basis. Our database is managed by AWS, which automatically patches all of the latest security updates.
Customer data is logically segregated using the monday.com Account ID.

marketplace_apps.description:
With CLI - Automate Actions, admins and project managers can perform bulk operations with simple commands, saving time and reducing risk of errors associated with manual, repetitive clicking. 


👋 Book a demo with us!


What is a CLI?

A CLI, or Command Line Interface, is a way to tell your computer what to do by typing commands instead of clicking icons. You type a command, press enter, and the computer responds by performing a task. Here, we bring that idea to monday.com.


Get the job done faster with commands, not clicks. 🚀

  • Add, remove, copy, or getinfo on a variety of monday.com elements such as workspaces, boards, groups, users, teams, and more!
  • Automating these tasks offers reduction in overall time and errors associated with constant manual clicking.


What types of work can this app help you with?

🗂️ Board setup for a new project

🖥️ Configuration and maintenance of monday.com

📊 Reporting and auditing

👤 User management

 

What are some specific tasks you can automate with this app?

🎨 Create and export lists of boards, workspaces, and users for an audit

👥 Add a new team or user to multiple workspaces at once

📑 Copy boards and items as project templates

🧹 Remove boards and groups in bulk to clean up your workspace and projects


In contrast to monday.com's automations that are event-based or triggered by actions, CLI - Automate Action is for ad-hoc tasks.


Countless automation possibilities

This app includes over 80 different actions you can execute from the command line, creating seemingly endless potential automations to free up your time.

 

Never used a command line before? No problem!

Writing commands is easy-peasy. Each command contains two parts:

  1. Action - the action to be performed, like exporting, saving, adding, or removing
  2. Parameters - the specific details to go along with the action, like what file to export to, what filter to apply, what boards to take action on, etc.

Find more information in our documentation here.

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: Upscale is a part of the Adaptavist Group Ltd. The Adaptavist Group Ltd has passed the ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification standard with SoA v. 2.0.

Yes, the app sends only non-customer-submitted data outside of monday.com. This includes information such as account ID, board ID, and user ID. We use this data solely to improve the service, monitor usage, and identify errors.
us-east-1
DynamoDB (AWS) - us-east-1

Adaptavist is committed to working with you to ensure compliance with all applicable laws and regulations concerning the protection of Personal Data. Should you have further queries with regard to this Policy, please contact us at contractuals@adaptavist.com.

HIPAA requirements do not normally apply to Upscale and its products, since we do not store or process protected health information (PHI). As such, a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) is not required.
Upscale is a part of the Adaptavist Group Ltd. The Adaptavist Group has a SOC 2 Type 2 report, audited and published by Deloitte.

The only redirects we do are to Oauth flows for Slack and monday.com. We use built in features of Oauth 2.0 to ensure that the redirected location is valid and the intended location. Such as state parameters and registered redirect URLs.
There are no attack vectors in our app where this could be exploited.

When the information is sent to any tracing tool (Sentry and Segment) the information is pseudo-anonymised. Therefore, only the user or account ID is sent, and all the information that can be sensitive is discarded or hidden.
Our access to systems requires two-step verification to ensure our account is secure and no one else can access resources even if our password is stolen.

In general, various people within the Adaptavist Group may need access to the information that you provide us. They may need this for technical, commercial or compliance reasons, and this will be done in accordance with Adaptavist Group’s internal access control policy.

We use React/Next.js and by using React components for the inputs, all data is sanitized and validated before being accepted. There is only 1 text input in our app for specifying the name of a Slack channel, which is very easy to sanitize and validate as to whether it is a valid Slack channel name or not.

Our board view front end app can only be loaded within a monday.com iframe. Attempting to load any app content from anywhere else will fail. We use CSP and STS headers to ensure no scripts can be injected and only valid, signed, requests from our front end are accepted by our backend API.

Incident is reported to customers affected as soon as possible, maximum within 72 hours. Incident is reported to appsupport@monday.com as soon as possible, within 24 hours. If Adaptavist is controller to the information breached (not only processor) regulatory authorities are notified, same time limits apply.  As an ISO 27001 certified Adaptavist Group has a group level incident process and a deticated Breach Process
We have an audit script that runs everytime we build and deploy and flags moderate or higher vulnerabilities that are prioritized and fixed right away.
We use a key design in DynamoDB that logically segregates customer data per account and user.

Test updates in a separate branch or staging environment before deploying to production.

-  Backend (Rails, Redis, and Sidekiq):
Manage gems with Bundler.
Regularly update gems and Rails using version constraints in the Gemfile.
Apply security patches promptly following announcements from the Rails Security Team.
Enable automatic deployment via Heroku CI/CD pipeline triggered by Git pushes.
Update the Redis add-on on Heroku through the Dashboard or CLI.
Receive automatic notifications from Heroku regarding necessary updates and maintenance.
Regularly update the Sidekiq gem using Bundler.
Monitor Sidekiq releases and security advisories.
Employ a rolling restart strategy to minimize service disruptions during updates.

- GitHub:
Leverage Dependabot for automated dependency updates, including GitHub Actions workflows.
Regularly review and merge pull requests generated by Dependabot to apply updates.
Extended PRs review, trunk-based branching strategy, limited access the staging/prod branches

deploying/releasing updates only after CI passed - both backend & frontend tests

Critical severity issues to be fixed within 4 weeks of being reported;

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: Strict access controls are in place to ensure that the user can only access the data that they have access to.

In our monday app page it's manually at the time of publishing a new version of app. When we lead the user to ScriptRunner Connect (SRC), makes use of serverless technologies, hence the patching of operating systems and other software on these levels are the responsibility of the serverless service vendor. SRC does utilize vulnerability scanning for third party software dependencies. All vulnerabilities regardless of their criticality are attended immediately after the discovery.

As ISO 27001 compliant product we adhere to the Adaptavist Group incident management process. Incident is reported to customers affected as soon as possible, maximum within 72 hours. Incident is reported to appsupport@monday.com as soon as possible, within 24 hours. If Adaptavist is controller to the information breached (not only processor) regulatory authorities are notified, same time limits apply.  As an ISO 27001 certified Adaptavist Group has a group level incident process and a deticated Breach Process.

In our monday app page, the application doesn't rely on any server-side processing and solely operates within monday's iframe, utilizing only the monday.com SDK to make requests, it is inherently secure against CSRF. SRC was recently penetration tested by a CREST certified vendor, no attack surfaces related to CSRF were found.

In our monday app page we don’t accept any user supplied parameters. We use react and all parameters are sanitized. SRC was recently penetration tested by a CREST certified vendor, no attack surfaces related to CSRF were found.

In general, various people within the Adaptavist Group may need access to the information that you provide us. They may need this for technical, commercial or compliance reasons, and this will be done in accordance with Adaptavist Group’s internal access control policy. On SRC, access to customer data is highly restricted for SRC team only.
MFA is enforced

When the information is sent to any tracing tool (Sentry and Segment) the information is pseudo-anonymised. Therefore, only the user or account ID is sent, and all the information that can be sensitive is discarded or hidden. PII data is anonymised and secrets are not logged.
SRC backend does not make use of models that would accept parameters that are not designed to be sent from the frontend. And our monday app page N/A as it is frontend only with no backend.
Adaptavist is Soc2 compliant
security@adaptavist.com
SRC aims to be penetration tested once per year

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: hey, we are not storing any information from the customer in the database of the app because our app is only a receipt and we are doing the calculation in real time using the short lived token.

we are using the Amazon API Gateway in the front of our servers and if needed we deploy on a second server and we migrate the endpoints that need to be migrated (for big changes) and for the security updates and small fixes we have in place CI/CD processes.


for security patches our time frame policy is:
Critical  vulnerabilities- 3-7 days after vulnerability alert released.
High vulnerabilities - 3-7 days after vulnerability alert released.
Medium vulnerabilities - 28 days after vulnerability alert released.
Low vulnerabilities - Next scheduled system upgrade (not to exceed 90 days).
If we discover a security breach our CTO or DPO will notify monday.com via email or any other provided method of notification.
our app is a receipt, based on this we are allowing only monday.com signed requests.
our app do not process any user supplied parameters, all our parameters are coming from monday.com.
as we do not store any information from the customer in the database, none has access to the customer data.
they only way of accessing our app servers is via SSH and this can be done only from the office IP or over VPN, no password is used for this only the approved keys can access the servers.

the code that takes care of the logging was audited by multiple developers so we could make sure that no secrets are logged, for the fields like email and phone number we are masking the information in the logs.

Crunchbase will promptly and properly notify customers, partners, users, affected parties, and regulatory agencies of relevant incidents or breaches under Crunchbase policies, contractual commitments, and regulatory requirements.

To protect all state-changing actions against CSRF, we use an xsrf_token cookie validated server-side. For each browser session, a unique token is generated and included in all state-changing requests. When such a request is received, the server verifies the token in the request against the token stored in the session.

Our application minimizes the need for explicit XSS encoding on the client side as we primarily use React for UI rendering, which inherently escapes HTML to prevent XSS attacks. React's design ensures that any user input rendered in the UI is automatically encoded, thus mitigating the risk of XSS by controlling the execution of potentially malicious scripts. We consciously avoid scenarios where unescaped user input might be directly inserted into the DOM, primarily through practices like dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
We implement comprehensive sanitization measures for all user input on the server side. This is to further safeguard against XSS and prevent the storage and propagation of incorrect or malicious data within our system. Our server-side sanitization process removes potentially harmful scripts or tags from the input before it is processed, stored, or sent back to the client for rendering.
By leveraging React's built-in protection against XSS on the client side and enforcing strict sanitization rules on the server side, we maintain a robust defense against XSS attacks across our application.

Crunchbase provides access to customer data only to those employees who have a job-related need to access such data, based on the ‘least privilege’ principle. Access to systems is requested, approved, and managed using Lumos.

Only selected members of selected teams have access to customer data, and only as required by their role. Crunchbase provides access to personal data only to those who have a job-related need to access such data, based on the ‘least privilege’ principle. Access to systems is requested, approved, and managed using Lumos.
MFA is required by policy for all remote access to the corporate network, and all exceptions to the policy are documented.
N/A, this is not specifically restricted.

The app mitigates mass parameter assignment attacks through a method akin to Data Transfer Objects (DTO). This approach ensures that each request processes only explicitly required information, effectively ignoring any additional, unexpected parameters.
Additionally, the app embeds these details within JSON Web Tokens (JWT) to secure sensitive information such as user or account IDs. These tokens are securely transmitted, as the secret key used for signing the JWTs is strictly shared between monday.com and our application, ensuring no external party can tamper with or fabricate valid tokens.

The app strategically uses redirects primarily within the authentication flows involving monday.com and, when necessary, Crunchbase. To ensure security and integrity in these redirects, the app employs the following measures:
Authentication Flow: The app leverages the authentication flow provided by monday.com. During this process, monday.com initiates a POST request to our backend. This request is securely signed with a Client Secret, which is confidentially stored within both monday.com and our backend's security storage. This verification step ensures that the request originates from a trusted source.
Hardcoded Links: The URLs the app redirects for token acquisition (either from monday.com or Crunchbase) are hardcoded within our application's codebase. This approach eliminates the risk of unauthorized redirects as the destinations are predefined and reviewed for security.
Token Handling: It's important to note that tokens are not directly involved in the redirect URLs. Instead, they are securely set through separate callbacks, minimizing exposure to potential redirect vulnerabilities.
Return URL Verification: After obtaining the necessary information through the authentication flow, the app redirects users using parameters received from monday.com. While the back URL itself is not explicitly verified against an allow list, we rely on the robust mechanism that only requests signed by monday.com can proceed through this authentication and redirection process. This implicit trust model is based on the secure exchange and verification of signed requests, ensuring that only authorized and intended redirections occur.

To the extent Crunchbase is required to comply with GDPR, the Crunchbase Data which is transferred to monday.com through the app complies with GDPR to the best of our knowledge. Please refer to the following for more information: https://about.crunchbase.com/terms-of-service/gdpr-privacy-policy/

Crunchbase was reviewed by an independent service provider during the SOC 2 Type II audit, which was completed in 2023. Security Review results summary and SOC II documents may be provided upon execution of an NDA via Crunchbase’s Whistic profile.

The limited metadata and configuration that we do store are secured behind a token that we generate for you. Only with that token can you access your own data only.

Our infrastructure relies on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) for server hosting and management, while our database is managed through MongoDB Atlas. Both GCP and MongoDB Atlas provide regular security updates and patches to safeguard our systems. Additionally, our team stays abreast of emerging vulnerabilities through continuous monitoring of industry sources and threat intelligence feeds. In response to new threats, we prioritize swift action, promptly applying patches and implementing mitigation measures to address any potential risks

Our team maintains regular communication with the monday.com team, covering various aspects such as features, bugs, and security best practices. In the event of a data breach that could impact monday.com, we prioritize immediate notification through our direct communication channels. We are committed to transparent collaboration, working closely with monday.com to swiftly address the breach and minimize any potential risks or data leakage.

We implement robust CSRF protection by securing all endpoints with tokens generated specifically for each user. These tokens, valid for a short period, act as a barrier against unauthorized state changes and data access. Without the valid token, any attempt to modify state or access data is rendered impossible, enhancing the security of our application
We prioritize protection against XSS attacks by adhering to best practices. This includes robust validation of user input and the use of official, up-to-date libraries when handling data

Access to customer data is strictly limited within our organization. Only authorized individuals are granted access, and they must use their private access credentials to log in. Access is granted on a need-to-know basis, ensuring that only those with a legitimate business requirement can access customer data

Our logging practices prioritize privacy, ensuring that personally identifiable information (PII) is never retained in our logs. Instead, we solely store IDs for pertinent log processing, maintaining a balance between data utility and user privacy.

We mitigate mass parameter assignment attacks by implementing strict input validations and utilizing libraries with built-in safeguards. These libraries enforce strong typing and parameter whitelisting, reducing the risk of unauthorized parameter manipulation

We employ a whitelist approach for redirection, allowing only trusted destinations specified in the whitelist. Any attempt to redirect to a destination outside of the whitelist is automatically rejected, accompanied by a relevant message to notify users

SuperMail does not directly subject to GDPR regulations as we do not store any sensetive information within our system. Only our help pages send the user to https://evolu.software/help/... to display the corresponding documentation
We do not use the post parameters directly. After validating the individual post parameters, each parameter is read individually using 'express-validator' matchedData.
We only log the names of the functions called, a success/failure and technical id(s)

We first use 'dompurify' and then 'express-validator' to check the data type of the parameters passed.

Yes, not necessary. Our app has integrations running in monday code. However, these are not called by the browser and are provided with a JWT (including a shortLivedToken) by monday.com. If no matching token was sent with a POST request, the request is rejected.

Number Column Without Commas is the very solution to your current problem of having to deal with annoying commas while storing numbers like years, postal codes, account numbers, company registration numbers, etc in your monday.com boards.


=> Although monday.com has no native way of doing this, this app achieves it in a clever way:

  1. For your existing number column, it generates a new text column and copies over all the existing number values to it.
  2. Next based on the 2-way sync between the original number column and text column, whenever you update a value in one column, it automatically updates into the other.
  3. As a result of this sync, you can hide your number column and work solely with the new column (without commas).
  4. In case you want to sort by the number, that is also easy, just set up the sort by the original number column and hide it. Now whenever you make changes to your new column (without commas), the value will update automatically in the hidden number column and so items/rows will remain sorted always.

=> To further understand how to use the app, checkout the demo video here


The app is absolutely free to try, so just scroll up and Add to your account to start using it :)

from time to time we do internal tests, as well as third party tests.

we check the url source and data, check that only request with additional data from monday are processed, for example, on the oAuth process, we make sure that the values at "response_type", "client_id", "scope", "state" are as expected from monday. we also redirect only after we validate the token with monday so it must be compatible with.

each parameter is taken exclusively and being checked before entering to DB, the monday code app is not even using a DB, only the secure storage, and there is no option to use Mass Assignment. 
in our backend, method are not taking permission values from a parameter, only by checking the authenticated user and decide from that, in addition to other restrictions.

logs are never containing secrets, tokens or passwords. for errors, we do log the internal userid so we can check and fix the error faster and accurate, and know who was affected to reach out with further updates.

only the main developer (founder) have access to the DB and sensitive data, including finance system etc. 

other employees have only access to basic information of the users like name, email, company name etc.. all signed on NDA and agreements before got access.

we are using best practices by the code we use: 
Frontend, angular: all data is sanitized by default. which means html and scripts are not being running from user data. 
backend: we use TypeORM for nodejs, with all the input parameters being sent as parameter to the SQL query using TypeORM query builder, which is protecting against SQL injection. 

We also passed the tests performed by monday marketplace team using burp suite software, as well as our own tests, and an external hacker that tried to hack but didn't succeed.

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: Customer data is segregated logically on the basis of Account ID. Account ID is retrieved from application session, application does not support other means of providing Account ID.

Application Frontend and Backend is built and deployed by a pipeline.
GitHub Dependabot is used to keep package dependencies up to date.
Every incident is reviewed and remediation actions are identified. Communicating security breach to monday.com is a part of the process.

All requests to backend are authenticated with monday.com session token.

1. Client-side, application uses the "monday-sdk-js" library to get the session token. This requires the main monday.com application to run. This token is sent to backend in the Authorization header.
2. Backend-side, application is verifying this token using monday client secret. Backend is configured with CORS settings for client origin only.

Application has 3 sources of user-provided data:

1. Integration 'prompt' text field

2. Table Item values

3. Results generated by processing ML prompts

The application has the following measures built-in:

1. All data from 'prompt' text is processed by https://github.com/cure53/DOMPurify library for sanitization (File: sanitization_prompt.png)

2. All data from table item values is processed by https://github.com/cure53/DOMPurify library. (File: sanitization_value.png)

3. All results, generated from ML prompts are processed by https://github.com/cure53/DOMPurify library for sanitization (File: sanitization_ml.png)

Application outputs data by updating column values. Before updating data in columns, application uses https://www.npmjs.com/package/validator library to encode HTML tags (using 'encode' function).

The company has only one employee.
The application only collects token usage per user and anonymized metrics.

Customer data is processed on AWS cloud. AWS Access is managed with SSO (AWS Identity Center) from Google Workspace.
Google workspace has 2-Factor authentication enforced.

AWS Root account has MFA set up.

Application logs are delivered to AWS Cloudwatch Logs log group. The log group has data protection policies enabled for automatic masking and reporting for all sensitive information findings.
Enabled policies: Credentials, Device Identifiers, PII, PHI, Financial information
The application does not have a user-facing interface (integrations + read-only dashboard)
The application does not have a user-facing interface which makes redirects (integrations + read-only dashboard)
The application is not storing PII or user data apart from usage information. Third-party processors are compliant with GDPR.

We deploy to monday Code using the monday Code CLI. We deploy a new version from our developer machines.

We can deploy in minutes but including time to find and fix issues we use the following SLA:
Critical: 1 business hour
Medium: 4 business hours
Low: 2 business days
Raise a support request and alert our CPM

The only state changing actions that take place are towards the monday.com API. We're using a combination of Typescript types, zod schemas and GraphQL Tada to generate a type safe way of creating queries and passing variables/parameters.
Only our development team has access to the app developer console, github (where our code is stored) and the logs in monday Code.
We use Google Authentication in front of most of the apps we use and have 2FA enforced on our Google Workspace accounts. For apps where this is not possible, we have also configured 2FA.

Our app doesn't work with PII other then the provided data through the integration requests (boardId/itemId/columnIds/etc). Secrets itself are never logged as we only use them in code files where we do not include the logger.
We use zod schema's to validate the incoming inputs for the requests we receive. If they contain information that doesn't match our expectations we return a 500 error.
Our app is a backend only so we don't redirect to anywhere and there's no need.

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: Yes, we have protocols in place to notify monday.com promptly in the event of a security breach. Upon detection, we assess the breach's impact and immediately take containment measures. monday.com is notified within 72 hours through their designated security channels, providing detailed information about the breach's nature, affected data, and containment actions. We maintain open communication for updates and follow-up actions. All incidents are documented thoroughly, with records available to monday.com upon request, ensuring a coordinated and transparent response to protect user data and integrity.

Yes, we enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all employees accessing systems that process or hold customer data. Our authentication method combines something the user knows (a password) with something the user has (a secure token or a smartphone app-generated code) to ensure a higher level of security. Before access is granted to any system containing customer data, employees are required to enter their unique password and a one-time code generated by their MFA device.. Additionally, we regularly review and update our security policies and training programs to ensure all team members understand the importance of security measures like MFA in protecting our systems and customer data.

ShortDay meticulously ensure that our logs do not contain secrets or Personally Identifiable Information (PII) by implementing a multifaceted approach. This includes configuring automated filters to scan and exclude sensitive information before logging, adhering to secure coding practices that prevent the logging of secrets and PII, and conducting regular audits to identify and address any lapses. Additionally, we use log sanitization tools to automatically strip out any sensitive data and enforce strict access control measures to limit log access to authorized personnel only. These comprehensive steps help safeguard the confidentiality and integrity of sensitive information within our systems.

These tests are performed semi-annually by an independent, certified third-party to simulate real-world attack scenarios. The testing scope includes web applications, network infrastructure, and endpoint security, helping us identify and remediate vulnerabilities effectively.

Yes, we have a process for installing application-level updates and security patches is applied in multiple steps of our development. We are using dependency tools to check for security issues - DependencyCheck, Sneak. Cannot create a new build unless the security issues are resolved. We also receive notifications about new vulnerabilities, assert the impact and actively fix the issue.
This involves reaching out to their security team via email or their designated incident reporting channels as outlined in our incident response plan.

All the requests to our backend api require a security header with a token generated by the monday SDK, obtained inside of the monday.com app iframe. There's no authentication or session data on the client side linked to our api URL.

We use Helmet security middleware in which provides XSS encoding and sanitization. See Helmet.js We validate user-supplied parameters on the backend. We also rely on the React.js library in which has built-in sanitization methods enabled by default.
Only the company's CTO has access to the database, and the access is only permitted for support and optimization purposes, with 2FA.
All our infrastructure implements 2FA, both our servers and our persistence providers require its use.
Code changes requires at least one team member to review it. It's part of the review process to make sure that no secrets neither PII will be logged.
The app protects against mass parameter assignment attacks by implementing strict an advanced input validation and sanitization techniques.

marketplace_apps.description:
Welcome to Portfolio and Project Management, your all-in-one solution for managing projects and optimizing portfolios effortlessly.


Key Features:


Project Portfolio Management: Gain a comprehensive overview of all your projects and portfolios in one place.


Gantt Chart Integration

  • Visualize Timelines and Roadmap: Easily see project timelines and dependencies, and visualize work on the Gantt view.
  • Dependency & Auto Scheduling: Automatically schedule tasks for efficiency, adjusting start dates based on dependent tasks.
  • Baselines: Set baselines to compare planned vs. actual progress.
  • Critical Paths: Identify critical tasks that impact project completion.
  • Milestones: Mark key points in your project.
  • Sync with monday.com: Keep everything updated across platforms.


Workload Management

  • Resource Allocation: Distribute tasks based on team availability to optimize productivity.
  • Capacity Planning: Balance team workloads to avoid overwork and ensure efficient progress.


Flexible pricing model

  • With our new pricing model, you only pay for users who actively use the app. Learn more about pricing here.


Experience the benefits of Portfolio and Project Management and enhance your project oversight and portfolio optimization.

For more details:﻿

▶️ Watch Demo Video | 📖 Get Started | ✉️ Help Center | 📆 Book a Demo | 📚 Customer Portal | 🔒Trust Center


TeamBoard Resource Planning and Time Tracking for monday.com

Tailored for teams seeking to optimize their processes and improve productivity, SLD offers a centralized hub where users can organize, document, and track SOPs associated with status labels in their monday.com boards.


Features and Benefits:

  • Effortless Organization ✅ - Easily list out labels of all status columns in a board in a separate board view, providing a comprehensive overview of workflow statuses and associated procedures.
  • Customizable Notes and Links ✅ - Add detailed notes and links to each status label, enabling users to document specific actions, instructions, or references related to individual labels.
  • Training and Onboarding Support ✅ - Facilitate training and onboarding processes by providing new team members with quick access to SOP documentation directly within the monday.com platform.
  • Increased Efficiency ✅ - Save time and reduce errors by standardizing SOP documentation and providing clear guidance on workflow procedures, ensuring consistency and accuracy across teams.
  • Improved Collaboration ✅ - Foster collaboration and knowledge sharing among team members by centralizing SOP documentation and enabling collaborative editing and feedback.

Examples of Use Cases:

  • A marketing team uses SLD to document standard procedures for campaign status updates, including specific tasks, timelines, and resource requirements.
  • A project management team utilizes SLD to outline SOPs for project milestones, providing detailed instructions and links to relevant project documents and resources.
  • A human resources department leverages SLD to enhance onboarding procedures for new employees.


Questions? Book a demo!

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: Our system employs a unified database architecture with logical segregation of customer data by company. Access controls are rigorously defined to ensure users can interact only with data pertinent to their specific company, safeguarding against unauthorised access to other companies' data. This logical data separation, upheld by precise role and permission management, ensures the confidentiality and integrity of customer information across our platform.

Our application-level updates and security patches are methodically applied to ensure system integrity and security. For vulnerabilities, our patching timeframes are as follows: Critical vulnerabilities are patched within 24 hours of identification; High vulnerabilities within 72 hours; Medium vulnerabilities within one week; and Low vulnerabilities within one month. This process is part of our commitment to maintaining a secure and reliable service, minimising potential risks to our clients and their data.

In case of a security breach, we would promptly notify monday.com following our incident response plan, which mandates immediate communication upon detection and confirmation of a breach. The notification, detailing the nature and scope of the breach, would be sent to the designated contact at monday.com as per our partnership agreement. This ensures timely and transparent handling of the incident, facilitating quick mitigation and corrective measures to protect all stakeholders involved.

Yes, our platform employs robust XSS (Cross-Site Scripting) encoding and sanitisation across all user-supplied parameters. This is effectively achieved through the utilisation of reactive forms in Angular 17, which automatically incorporates these security measures. Angular's reactive forms approach not only simplifies form handling but also significantly enhances security by automatically escaping user input. This means that any potentially harmful scripts inserted by users are neutralised before being processed or displayed, thereby preventing XSS vulnerabilities. By leveraging Angular 17's advanced features, we ensure a secure environment for our users, protecting both their data and our systems from XSS attacks without compromising on functionality or user experience.

To safeguard customer data from unauthorized access by non-classified employees, we've instituted stringent security measures:

Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Employees are granted access only to data essential for their roles, minimising unauthorised access risks.

Least Privilege Principle: Access levels are carefully assigned to ensure employees have only the minimal access needed for their job functions, effectively reducing the likelihood of data breaches.

Data Classification: Data is categorised based on sensitivity, with access restricted to those needing it for their roles, ensuring that sensitive information is tightly controlled.

Auditing and Monitoring: Regular audits and monitoring of data access patterns help detect unauthorised access, with anomalies investigated promptly.

Employee Training: Security awareness training is mandatory for all employees, emphasising the importance of our data protection policies and the proper handling of sensitive information.

Encryption and Anonymisation: We employ encryption for data at rest and in transit and use anonymisation where feasible to protect data integrity.

Physical Security: Robust physical security measures prevent unauthorised access to our facilities, protecting devices and networks storing customer data.

Security Assessments: Our security measures are regularly evaluated and updated in response to new threats, ensuring ongoing protection of customer data.

These comprehensive measures collectively safeguard customer data against unauthorised access by non-classified employees, maintaining our commitment to data security and customer trust.

We implement multi-factor authentication (MFA) to secure access to our systems and customer data in two distinct ways:

MFA for Physical Server Access: Physical access to servers that store and process customer data is secured with MFA. This means that any employee needing physical access must provide multiple forms of identification and authentication beyond just a key or access card. This layer ensures that even physical breaches require multiple security challenges, significantly reducing the risk of unauthorised access.

MFA for ZingHub Login: For digital access, particularly to our ZingHub platform, MFA is mandatory for all employees. This process requires them not only to enter their password but also to verify their identity through a second factor, such as a code sent to a mobile device or generated by an authenticator app. This step ensures that access to our digital resources is doubly protected, safeguarding sensitive customer data from cyber threats.

By applying MFA both to physical and digital realms, we significantly heighten our security posture, ensuring robust protection against unauthorised access and enhancing the overall security of customer data. This comprehensive approach to MFA is a testament to our commitment to maintaining the highest standards of data security.

In our ZingHub SaaS system, we diligently ensure logs are devoid of secrets, such as passwords and API keys, and personally identifiable information (PII). Adhering to stringent data protection standards and compliance requirements, our approach is twofold:

Prudent Data Handling: We practice data minimisation, ensuring logs capture only essential information. This minimises potential security risks associated with storing sensitive data.

Sanitisation and Masking: On occasions where logging specific details is necessary for operational efficiency, we employ sanitisation and masking. This process obscures sensitive segments of the data, rendering it secure for monitoring and troubleshooting without compromising privacy.

Our logging framework is designed with security at its core, featuring secure storage solutions, rigorous access control, and periodic audits to safeguard against inadvertent logging of sensitive information. Additionally, our proactive monitoring system swiftly flags potential issues, ensuring continuous protection of user data.

By upholding these robust logging practices, ZingHub guarantees the security and privacy of our clients' data, reinforcing our commitment to excellence in data stewardship.

Yes, our application is fortified against mass parameter assignment attacks, thanks to the design of our API which is characterised by its granularity. We employ atomic calls that are specifically tailored to update only designated values. This architecture ensures that each call is responsible for a singular, explicit action, thereby mitigating the risk of unintended mass updates or modifications to data fields. By adopting this approach, we effectively limit the scope of each request to the server, ensuring that only authorised changes are made, and maintain stringent control over the data fields that can be modified through the API. This methodical and precise control mechanism is pivotal in safeguarding our system against the potential vulnerabilities associated with mass parameter assignment.

Yes, our application ensures that redirects and forwards are securely managed by exclusively permitting destinations that are pre-approved and listed on an allow list. This is accomplished through the use of Angular's routing mechanism in our main application. Angular's routing framework allows us to define paths and associated components in a way that naturally incorporates security checks against unauthorised redirects. By leveraging Angular's capabilities, we ensure that any attempt to redirect or forward to a new page is validated against our allow list, effectively preventing navigation to potentially untrusted or harmful content. This approach not only enhances the security of our application but also maintains the integrity of user navigation, aligning with best practices for web application security.

Monday code handles runtime and OS patches automatically; we review dependency advisories weekly and redeploy with the latest versions.

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: In every applicable database table, account_id is kept as one of the fields, so that all the data belonging to an account is logically separated from other accounts.

We use Google Cloud Platform for infrastructure hosting and Cloudflare for web security and they manage all the application-level updates and security patches for their services. We maintain the application and security updates in our business logic code, and fix promptly whenever a vulnerability found in the nodejs packages we are using is publicly announced.
As and when we become aware of a security breach, we will instantly reach out to monday team (at appsupport@monday.com) and notify them.

We authenticate and authorize each request by verifying the JWT token sent in the request header. The JWT token is signed by monday using the client or signing secrets, and is thus a secure way of identifying the request sender.
We use React JS framework for our UI. Using React components for user input ensures that the supplied data is sanitized properly.
We have strict checks and policies as to who has access to our maintained data and infrastructure.
Access to our systems requires two-step authentication to ensure that our maintained data and infrastructure is safe and secure.
We do not log any secrets or PII. Everywhere in the code we access/retrieve items/records using account_id, user_id (which we get from monday) which is logged instead.
The only redirects we do are to Google OAuth page, and our trusted/owned infrastructure.

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: In our system, customer data is logically segregated using userId and accountId parameters. Each set of data is uniquely tied to these identifiers, ensuring that customer information is isolated and can only be accessed through authenticated and authorized sessions. This method effectively maintains data privacy and security.

For installing application-level updates and security patches, we follow a structured process:

Assessment: Identifying and assessing the updates or patches needed.
Testing: Applying updates in a controlled staging environment to test compatibility and functionality.
Approval: Reviewing test results and approving for production deployment.
Deployment: Implementing the updates during scheduled maintenance windows to minimize disruption.
Monitoring: Continuously monitoring the system for any issues arising from the updates.
We will notify monday via email and slack community, immediately.
we protect all state-changing actions against Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) by implementing industry-standard security practices

All user inputs are sanitized using libraries that strip out potentially malicious code.
We implement strict Content Security Policies (CSP) that restrict the sources of executable scripts, further reducing the risk of XSS attacks.
Nobody has access to the customer data, we have a system where employees request customer data if there is support ticket is received.
Every apps and google account of employees has enabled 2fa

Configure logging levels and contents meticulously to exclude sensitive data from being captured.
Conduct regular audits of log files and log handling practices to ensure compliance with data protection regulations and to identify any potential for accidental logging of sensitive data.
Validating all user inputs for correctness before processing.
Only destinations explicitly listed in a pre-defined allowlist are permitted for redirects and forwards, effectively blocking any unspecified URLs.

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer:
We store user data in the same table, but logically separate it through Row Level Security policies that enforce users to only be able to access their own data.
No user is able to select any other users' data, since all queries are routed and secured through PostgREST, which uses parametrization, among many other security prevention systems, to make sure the RLS in place checks for eventual malicious requests. In the evenience of one of those requests, RLS will still be enforced, so the user won't be able to access other users' data.

Every time a new version of Postgres/PostgREST/any other front or backend library gets published that solves a security issue, dependabot for the frontend or supabase for the backend will open a PR or notify us, so we can immediately update the server. We run migrations to automatically update and pack all kinds of vulnerabilities. This means we can patch vulnerabilities the very moment we receive the notification.

In case of a security breach, we have industry-standard SOPs and security-specific protocols in place that act as a todo list to make sure all involved parties know what's happening as soon as possible. This includes notifying monday through the app marketplace team of any security breach and collaborate to solve it as soon as possible.
Our frontend is hosted on Vercel that automatically ensures security on internal endpoint is top notch, and all our backend points of contact have CSRF checks in place.

While PostgREST automatically parametrizes all requests and checks authentication every time, we use JWTs for authentication, along with monday.com authentication tokens. We do have XSS protection in place, but we're still working on it.
Every employee at the company is under NDA. Nobody can access data without explicit authorization to access the postgresql web interface.

Every employee at our company has MFA set up on his GitHub, his Supabase account, his Netlify account, and his Vercel account. We use Dashlane or iCloud KeyChain to generate complex and secure passwords, and to save authentication codes. We also use biometric authentication when that's an option.
We don't need to ship secrets to the client, and all our server logging is done through Sentry, which automatically encrypts all secrets.

We use realtime websockets which are rate-limited and rate-controlled by nature. This means attackers can't "spam" http requests nor do any mass parameter assignment attacks. Any other realtime-related potential issues are handled for by supabase realtime.
We have a popup for all external clickable links that asks the user to confirm he wants to open said link on a new tab
We don't store cookies nor track users in any way, shape, or form.
We're working towards being SOC2 compliant and we expect it to happen within the next 6 months
We're working towards being HIPAA compliant and we expect it to happen within the next 6 months
security@sundaydevs.com

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: Our platform ensures customer data is isolated using logical segregation. The app operates as a multi-tenant application, implementing application-level isolation to ensure each customer's data remains private and secure.

We prioritize the installation of critical updates and security patches. Critical issues are addressed immediately upon discovery. High-severity vulnerabilities are remedied within 72 hours, medium within two weeks, and low-severity issues within a month, ensuring continuous protection against threats.

In the unfortunate event of a security breach, we promptly notify monday.com via email, detailing the breach's scope. Direct contact is also made with our monday.com representatives through the platform and by phone, especially with our London team, to guarantee rapid and effective communication.
Yes, we implement CSRF tokens to authenticate and validate all state-changing requests, effectively guarding against Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) attacks.
The user interface, developed with the React Framework, inherently mitigates common XSS vulnerabilities. We also use the library DOMPurify for all parameters.

Access to customer data is strictly limited to essential personnel, following the principle of least privilege. Our Chief Technology Officer (CTO) is the only individual with full access, which is secured through an encrypted key and a secure connection.

Yes, to access systems that process or contain customer data, employees must undergo multi-factor authentication. This includes the use of a password and a private key, enhancing the security and privacy of customer data.
Yes, our logging practices are designed to exclude secrets and personally identifiable information (PII). We adhere to best practices for log management, limiting log entries to essential parameters.

We protect against mass parameter assignment attacks by adhering to best practices that restrict object access to authenticated tokens. These tokens are precisely tailored to possess only the necessary permissions for the intended operations.
There are no redirects or forwards in our app.
See https://www.docexport.com/security/
Johannes Geyer - jg@towerapps.com

We use CI/CD Dev/Sec/Ops with GitLab and Containers to automatically patch and upgrade our containers that run Q-ARGH.
