marketplace_apps.description:
Automation Scheduler brings proactive automation to monday.com. (Free to use while in early release!)


Native monday.com automations are reactive, running only when something changes on an individual item. Automation Scheduler enables teams to run scheduled, criteria-based automation across an entire board. Instead of waiting for an event to happen, Automation Scheduler periodically scans your board, finds items that match defined filter conditions, and executes automation sequences automatically.

Get a demo of Automation Scheduler →


How it works

Automation Scheduler uses a simple two-part model:


Filter Recipes - Define which items should be processed using reusable, pre-built filters such as:

  • Status + date combinations
  • Status + number values
  • Time tracking conditions
  • Last updated or inactivity checks
  • Completed or not completed logic

Filters can run on a daily, weekly, monthly schedule, or on demand via button click.


Action Recipes - Create reusable automation sequences using monday.com’s standard automation actions, including:

  • Status changes
  • Notifications
  • Item moves
  • Date updates
  • Any third-party actions available through custom automations

Once a filter finds matching items, the selected action sequence runs across all of them in one pass.


What this enables

Automation Scheduler makes it possible to automate workflows that were previously manual or unreliable, including:

  • Daily scans for overdue or stalled work
  • Automated cleanup of completed items
  • Enforcement of time tracking rules
  • Alerts for items that haven’t been updated recently
  • Consistent rule enforcement across large boards


Why teams use Automation Scheduler

  • Reduce manual board maintenance
  • Prevent work from quietly slipping through the cracks
  • Keep data accurate as teams and boards scale
  • Extend monday.com automations without replacing them


Automation Scheduler helps ensure your boards stay clean, predictable, and reliable over time. Book a demo →

marketplace_apps.description:
Out of Office Assistant keeps work moving when teammates are away by automatically posting clear updates, routing ownership to backups, and replying when an OOO user is @mentioned.


Free 14-day trial • Setup in minutes • Rule-based

How it works (3 steps)

  1. Each user sets OOO dates and chooses a global backup person
  2. Admin selects the Owner (People) column and sets board behavior
  3. When the owner is OOO, the app posts updates, notifies the right people, and can route work to the backup


Key features

Per-user OOO + backup (global)

Users set start/end dates and pick a backup once—applies across boards in the account.

Board rules: Warn or Auto-reassign

Admins control behavior per board:

  • Warn: keep owner unchanged and post a clear update
  • Auto-reassign: move ownership to the backup to prevent blocked work


Safe behavior on private boards

If the backup isn’t a subscriber (no access), the app won’t break permissions— it posts an update and keeps the owner unchanged.


Custom update templates (placeholders)

Create messages using placeholders like:

{assigned_user}, {backup_user}, {ooo_end}


@Mention auto-reply (with rate limits)

When someone @mentions a user who is OOO, the app can auto-reply with the backup contact. Built-in rate limits prevent noisy repeated replies.


Conflict-free backup selection

Users who are currently out of office are excluded from backup choices to avoid routing to unavailable people.


Problems this solves

  • Work stuck with unavailable owners
  • Manual reassignment during leave and holidays
  • Unclear coverage and missed follow-ups
  • Repeated pings to teammates who are away


Ideal for

Support & Ops ticketing, project delivery, incident response, and any team that needs reliable backup ownership during absences.

Need help getting started? Book a personal demo, or contact us for any questions at support@lanceops.com.

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: Application logs are stored securely within the cloud hosting provider’s logging system (Render). Logs are used solely for operational monitoring and debugging.
Application data is stored in a managed PostgreSQL database. Data is encrypted at rest and access is restricted to server-side services.

The app strictly restricts redirects and forwards to approved, predefined destinations only.

All redirects are controlled server-side and limited to trusted domains owned and operated by PermitNerd or monday.com. The app does not allow user-supplied redirect URLs, dynamic forwarding, or redirection to external or untrusted content.

This ensures users are never redirected to malicious or unintended destinations and aligns with monday.com security and compliance best practices.

The app explicitly whitelists and validates allowed request parameters on the server side. Only expected, predefined fields are processed, and any additional or unexpected parameters are ignored. This prevents mass parameter assignment and unauthorized modification of protected fields.

Logs are intentionally designed to exclude secrets, access tokens, and personally-identifiable information. Sensitive credentials are stored securely in environment variables and never written to logs.

Access to production systems and infrastructure is restricted to the developer and protected using provider-level security controls, including multi-factor authentication (MFA) enforced by hosting and tooling providers (e.g., GitHub, cloud hosting, and database services).

Access to customer data is limited to the minimum required for application functionality. Service-role credentials are used only on secure server-side routes, tokens are scoped per account, and no customer data is exposed to unauthorized users or clients.

All user-supplied input is validated and sanitized before processing or storage. The app does not render raw user input as executable code, and responses are served as structured JSON. Client-side rendering follows safe encoding practices to prevent Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).

All state-changing actions are protected using authenticated requests and verified tokens. The app relies on monday.com session tokens, server-side authorization checks, and webhook signature verification to ensure requests originate from trusted sources and cannot be forged.

The developer maintains incident response procedures and monitoring mechanisms. In the event of a security incident affecting monday.com users or data, monday.com would be notified promptly in accordance with platform requirements and responsible disclosure best practices.
Customer data is logically segregated by monday account ID. All queries are scoped per account, ensuring that customers can only access their own data.

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: The app does not send any data outside of monday.com.

The app stores log data securely on our server. Access to these logs is restricted to authorized personnel and is used solely for monitoring, debugging, and ensuring the proper functioning of the application.

The app stores all application data securely on our server. Access is restricted to authorized personnel, and the data is protected using appropriate security measures to ensure confidentiality and integrity.
We have a dedicated security and privacy point of contact for such issues or questions.
The app does not forward to any unapproved destinations.

The app protects against mass parameter assignment attacks. Only explicitly allowed fields are bound to data models or database operations. Input is whitelisted or validated server-side, and sensitive fields such as roles, permissions, and internal IDs are never exposed to the client or modifiable via user input.

The developer ensures that application logs do not contain secrets or personally identifiable information (PII). All console and log statements are reviewed before deployment to confirm that no confidential or sensitive data is included in the logs.

We enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all employee access to systems that may process customer data. MFA is enabled for signing in to our servers, ensuring that access requires both a password and a second authentication factor to enhance security.

Access to customer data is protected based on the principle of least privilege. Employees and services are granted only the minimum level of access necessary to perform their specific roles. Access controls are reviewed periodically to ensure that permissions remain appropriate and unnecessary access is promptly removed.

The app performs input sanitization and output encoding to protect against Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks. We ensure that any user-supplied input is validated and sanitized before processing or storing, and HTML encoding is applied when displaying user data in the frontend. We also use secure libraries/frameworks that automatically escape outputs in templates and prevent script injection.

All state-changing actions are protected against Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF). The app implements CSRF tokens for all forms and API endpoints that modify state. These tokens are validated server-side, and only requests with valid, trusted tokens are processed.
We have a mechanism to notify monday.com in the event of a security breach.

The developer follows a defined process for regularly applying application-level updates and security patches. This includes:

- Monitoring official sources (e.g., package managers, vendor advisories) for updates.

- Periodically updating software packages, libraries, and dependencies.

- Applying database security patches in coordination with the infrastructure team.

- Using automated tools (e.g., Dependabot, npm audit, pip-audit, etc.) to detect vulnerabilities.

- Testing updates in a staging environment before deployment to production.

Customer data is logically segregated from the data of other customers. This is achieved through the use of unique identifiers (IDs) for each customer, ensuring that their data is kept separate and secure.

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer:
The app sends zero requests to external domains. All API communication goes exclusively through the monday.com SDK. There are no analytics services, no external CDNs, no ad platforms, no monitoring tools, and no third-party integrations! 

All data remains within monday.com's infrastructure.

The app is client-side only. Logs are output to the browser console via a centralised logging utility and are not persisted or transmitted anywhere. 

In production, only error-level logs are output. No log data is stored on any server or external service.
The app stores all data exclusively in monday.storage.instance, which is monday.com's built-in key-value storage infrastructure. No external databases, no localStorage, no cookies.

Security and privacy inquiries can be directed to Proof via the contact email provided in the app listing. 

Response time is within 24 hours per the monday.com SLA requirements.

Pulse is designed with GDPR compliance in mind. All data stays within monday.com and when the app is uninstalled, monday.com automatically handles the lifecycle of instance storage, removing all app data.

User names and emails are fetched live for display purposes only, held in memory, and never persisted.

A privacy policy is published at proof.engineering/privacy.
Pulse does not perform any external redirects. It runs entirely within monday.com's iframe and all navigation stays within the monday.com platform.
The app has no server-side API endpoints that accept arbitrary parameters. There are no object-spread assignments from raw user input.
The app requests only the minimum scopes necessary for its functionality and nothing else.

Multiple layers of protection are implemented such as:

All user-facing data is rendered through React's JSX, which automatically escapes HTML entities. 

Pulse removes HTML tags and decodes entities from activity log data before display.

Our CSV export prevents injection by escaping fields containing commas, quotes, newlines, or formula characters.

Activity Pulse uses monday.com storage exclusively for all data persistence. 

Instance storage is automatically scoped to the installing account by monday.com's infrastructure. Each installation has its own isolated storage namespace. The app has no external database or shared data store. Customer data cannot cross between accounts.

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: Yes. The app sends data to our backend service hosted on Google Cloud Platform (Cloud Run). The data sent includes non-customer-submitted identifiers (account ID, board ID, item ID, user ID) as well as limited customer-submitted content (worklog, descriptions, leave request notes, and user-defined names for saved views, reports, holidays, and capacity schemes).
Application logs are stored in Google Cloud Logging (GCP).
App data is stored in a PostgreSQL database hosted on Google Cloud Platform (Cloud SQL).
Our team has a dedicated point of contact for security and privacy inquiries. Security issues can be reported to support@reinwok.com and will be triaged within 24 hours.

The app is designed with GDPR principles in mind. We minimize data collection by storing primarily monday.com identifiers rather than personal data - user names and personal details are fetched in real-time from the monday.com API and are not persisted. Customer data is logically isolated using PostgreSQL Row-Level Security. All data is hosted on Google Cloud Platform infrastructure within GDPR-compliant regions. Data is encrypted at rest and in transit. The app supports data deletion upon account uninstallation to fulfill right-to-erasure requirements.

All redirects in our application are restricted to approved destinations. OAuth flows redirect only to hardcoded monday.com authorization endpoints, and post-authentication redirects use server-configured environment variables — no user-supplied URLs are used for redirection.

We use NestJS global ValidationPipe with strict whitelisting (whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true). All endpoints enforce typed DTOs with class-validator decorators, rejecting any unexpected properties in request payloads.

Our logging implementation uses structured logging that captures request metadata, error details, and operational events without logging authentication tokens, session secrets, or personally-identifiable information. Sensitive headers (Authorization, X-Monday-Token) are not included in log output. Logs contain only operational data such as request paths, status codes, error messages, and tenant account IDs. Additionally, we have automated checks in our merge process to detect and prevent any accidental logging of sensitive data before code reaches production.

We enforce multi-factor authentication on all systems that process or have access to customer data, including our Google Cloud Platform console, GitHub repositories. MFA is required for all team members with access to production infrastructure and databases.

Access to production customer data is restricted based on the principle of least privilege. Our Google Cloud Platform IAM roles are scoped to grant only the minimum permissions required for each team member's role. Direct access to the
production database is limited to essential personnel only. Application secrets and credentials are managed through GCP Secret Manager with access controls. No production customer data is used in development or testing environments.

Backend validates and constrains all user input via class-validator DTOs. Frontend sanitizes all external data using DOMPurify with zero allowed HTML tags/attributes (plain text only). No unsafe rendering patterns (innerHTML, eval) are used.

Our application uses stateless JWT-based authentication via Authorization headers (Bearer tokens). Since tokens are not stored in cookies and must be explicitly attached to each request, the application is inherently protected against CSRF attacks. All state-changing actions require a valid session token verified against monday.com's signing secret.

We have structured logging via GCP Cloud Logging for security event monitoring. In case of a detected security breach, we will notify monday.com's security team promptly via the designated partner communication channels, including details of the incident scope and remediation steps

We maintain a regular process for reviewing and applying security patches to all application dependencies and infrastructure. Our application is containerized (Docker) and deployed on Google Cloud Run, enabling rapid deployment of security updates. Dependencies are regularly audited and updated

Yes. Customer data is logically segregated using PostgreSQL Row-Level Security (RLS) policies. Every data table includes an account_id column, and RLS policies enforce that each tenant can only access rows matching their own account_id. The tenant context is set at the database session level via middleware after JWT authentication, ensuring data isolation is enforced at the database layer - not just the application layer.

Customer Voice turns a monday.com board into a public feedback portal so customers and teammates can submit ideas, vote, and follow what’s being considered - while you manage everything where you already work.


With Customer Voice you can

  • Publish a board as a branded portal to collect feedback from anyone
  • Let users upvote and comment to signal priority and demand
  • Accept new idea submissions via a simple intake form
  • Keep a single source of truth: every request becomes an item on your board
  • Triage, prioritize, and update status using your existing board workflow


Common use cases

  • Feature requests portal for SaaS products
  • Bug/issue intake with voting to spot recurring pain points
  • Customer advisory feedback hub for roadmap planning
  • Internal idea board for teams to propose and prioritize improvements


How it works

  • Start with a board template with preconfigured board and columns
  • Choose your portal setup: pick your URL, set a page title + description, add your logo, and customize theming to match your brand.
  • Publish when ready: make board data publicly accessible to anyone with the link.
  • Board ↔ Portal sync: every item on your board becomes a votable, discussable entry on the portal.
  • Frictionless participation: no monday account required to comment, vote, or submit.


What you get

  • A single source of truth: all feedback is stored as items in your monday board
  • Capture demand with voting and comments to help prioritize faster
  • Create as many portals as you like: one board = one portal
  • Fit it into your existing workflow: no separate standalone tool to maintain

Please note, that the public feedback page currently loads up to 500 ideas from the connected monday board. If your board has more than 500 items, only the first 500 are shown on the public page for now.


Demo

Leave your details here and we’ll reach out to schedule a demo.


Documentation

Learn more and see setup guide: https://customer-voice.app

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: The app is hosted entirely on Monday Code, which is covered by monday.com's ISO 27001 certification (trust.monday.com).

The app sends Google file IDs, permission roles, and OAuth tokens to Google APIs to operate the embed functionality. Anonymous, cookieless usage analytics are sent to PostHog. No board names, item names, or document content are ever sent outside monday.com.
Logs are stored in Monday Code's built-in logging infrastructure, covered by monday.com's SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certifications.

All app data — OAuth tokens, view configuration, and secrets — is stored exclusively on monday.com's platform via Monday SecureStorage, Storage API, and SecretsManager. No external database or third-party storage is used.

The app runs on Monday Code, which is covered by monday.com's annual third-party penetration testing program. At the application level, we conduct ongoing security audits and automated penetration testing using AI-powered security agents that review the codebase for OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities, authentication weaknesses, and insecure data handling. Application dependencies are continuously scanned via npm audit and GitHub Dependabot, and identified issues are remediated before each release.
Security inquiries: security@bam-apps.com. Privacy inquiries: privacy@bam-apps.com.
The app is not independently HIPAA certified and does not offer a Business Associate Agreement (BAA). It is not designed to process protected health information.

The app runs on monday.com's GDPR-compliant platform and stores all data exclusively on Monday infrastructure. Tokens are deleted on disconnect, all data is purged on uninstall, and the app uses no cookies. Data subject requests can be directed to privacy@bam-apps.com.

The app's only redirect is to Google's official OAuth endpoint (accounts.google.com). The OAuth callback origin is encoded in an HMAC-signed PKCE state parameter and validated with a timing-safe comparison before use, preventing tampering or open-redirect attacks. No user-supplied URLs are ever used in any redirect or forward.
All API routes explicitly extract and validate individual properties from request bodies. Request bodies are never spread or passed directly to storage.
Logs contain only non-PII identifiers and operation outcomes. OAuth tokens, email addresses, and user names are never logged.
MFA is enforced on all systems with access to app configuration.

Google OAuth uses the minimal drive.file scope, which restricts the app to only the files a user explicitly selects through the Google Drive Picker — the app cannot browse, list, or access any other files in the user's Drive. monday.com scopes are read-only (me:read, account:read). All stored data is scoped to the authenticated user, and only the embed owner can modify settings.
The React frontend uses JSX auto-escaping with no dangerouslySetInnerHTML usage. All user inputs are sanitized server-side and the app never renders user-supplied HTML.
The app uses Bearer token authentication and sets no cookies, so browser-based CSRF attacks cannot forge valid requests. The Google OAuth flow uses PKCE with HMAC-signed state.
We maintain an incident response process that includes notifying monday.com within 72 hours of any confirmed breach. Reports can be initiated at security@bam-apps.com.
Monday Code handles all infrastructure-level patching automatically. Application dependencies are monitored via GitHub Dependabot and patched before each release.
Monday Code provides infrastructure isolation between accounts. At the application level, all stored data uses composite keys scoped by account ID and user ID, ensuring complete logical isolation.

monday.com now supports 5 levels of subitems. 


Native automations don't follow you down there — so every deep hierarchy becomes a copy-paste job, updating the same status across 40 subitems by hand.


Multi Level Subitem Automations fixes that. Real automations across all 5 levels — 100% native, no Zapier, no Make.


In short:

✅ Run automations at any level — top item down to the deepest subitem.

✅ Sync parent values down to all 5 subitem levels, automatically.

✅ Copy entire subitem trees with all column values mapped.

✅ Convert any subitem into a top-level item on any board.

✅ Auto-name subitems with the parent's name as prefix or suffix.


— What You Can Automate —


Sync values across all 5 subitem levels

When a parent item column changes, sync the new value to every subitem automatically. No more manual copy-paste.


Set default subitem values

When a new subitem is created, automatically copy a parent column value onto it.

Assign the owner, sync statuses, dates priorities and timelines — all on creation.


Create subitems from a template (on creation & change).

When an item or subitem is created or status changes, copy all subitems from a chosen board to the new item/subitem and values are mapped across boards by name and type.


Convert subitems to items.

Promote any subitem into a standalone item on any board, with column values mapped during the move.


Auto-name subitems with a parent prefix or suffix.

Prepend or append the parent's name with a custom connector. Keeps nested work readable in lists, exports, and dashboards.


Built for monday.com's multi-level boards

Only works on multi-level boards — monday.com's new board type with 5 subitem levels. Cross-board column mapping for files, tags, and all standard columns.


Enterprise-Grade Security

Built on monday.com's native code platform with no data storage and full compliance, ensuring the highest level of security, compliance, and reliability. With no external servers involved, your data remains fully protected within monday.com’s infrastructure, meeting stringent enterprise-grade security standards.


— Who It's For —

  • Teams who gave up on Zapier because the subitem logic got too deep
  • Anyone who's said "I'll update these manually this once" then did it 40 times
  • Projects where one date change cascades to 30 nested subitems


Feedback? Questions? Requests?

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: we are not ISO/IEC 27001 certified. However, our app minimizes security risk by design: it is a client-side only application with no backend, no database, and no external data storage. All data remains within monday.com's own ISO 27001-certified infrastructure.

Our app does not send any data outside of monday.com. It is a client-side only application running within the monday.com iframe. All communication is exclusively between the app and monday.com's GraphQL API via the Monday SDK. No data is sent to any third-party service, external server, or analytics platform.

Logs are stored exclusively in the browser's localStorage on the user's device (client-side only). They are kept in a circular buffer (max 5,000 entries) and never sent to any external server or third-party service. Logs can be exported manually as JSON by the user via a debug panel for troubleshooting purposes. No log data leaves the user's browser.

All app data is stored using monday.com's native infrastructure. Board data (groups, items, subitems) is managed through monday.com's GraphQL API. App-specific settings (board designation, onboarding state, review prompt tracking) are stored using monday.com's Storage API (monday.storage). No external database or vendor-hosted storage is used.

Our app is a client-side only board view with no backend server, no database, and no external data storage. All communication goes directly to Monday.com's GraphQL API via the Monday SDK within the iframe. Given this minimal attack surface (no server infrastructure to test), we have not performed formal penetration testing.
Security and privacy inquiries can be directed to hello@sorobu.io.

Our app is not HIPAA compliant. It is a general-purpose mind mapping tool that does not process, store, or transmit any protected health information (PHI). All data resides within monday.com's infrastructure.

we do not hold SOC 2 or SOC 3 certification. Our app has no backend infrastructure to audit — it is a client-side only application where all data processing and storage is handled by monday.com's own SOC 2-certified infrastructure.

Our app is GDPR compliant by design. It does not collect, store, or process any personal data independently — all data remains within monday.com's infrastructure. The app has no backend, no database, no cookies, no analytics, and no third-party tracking. Local browser logs (localStorage) contain only operational data and can be cleared by the user at any time. For any data-related requests, users can contact us at hello@sorobu.io.

Our app does not perform any redirects or forwards. It runs entirely within the Monday.com iframe as a client-side board view, communicating only with Monday.com's GraphQL API via the Monday SDK. There are no external URLs or user-controlled redirect targets.

Our app has no backend server or database. It is a client-side only application running within the Monday.com iframe. All data mutations are performed through Monday.com's GraphQL API using specific, explicitly defined fields — there is no server-side object binding or ORM that could be vulnerable to mass assignment.

Logs are stored locally in the user's own browser (localStorage) and are never transmitted externally. Log entries contain only operational data: session IDs (randomly generated), board IDs, log categories, and action descriptions. No passwords, tokens, API keys, email addresses, or personal names are stored in logs. The userId field contains only the monday.com numeric user ID (not names or emails), and it is only accessible to the user themselves within their own browser session.

MFA is enabled on GitHub, which hosts the source code repository and CI/CD pipeline. As a client-side only app with no backend or database, there is no server infrastructure processing customer data. The app runs entirely within the monday.com iframe, and customer data is managed by monday.com's own security infrastructure.

Our app follows the principle of least privilege at multiple levels:

API scopes: The app only requests the monday.com API scopes strictly necessary for its board view functionality (reading and writing board data).
Viewer gating (ADR-025): Users with "Viewer" role are detected at the source and blocked from all API calls — no data is fetched or exposed to unauthorized users.
No backend/no storage: The app does not store, cache, or persist any customer data outside of monday.com. All data remains within monday.com's infrastructure.

Our app is built with React, which automatically escapes all rendered content by default, preventing XSS through DOM injection. All user input (node labels) is passed to Monday.com's GraphQL API using parameterized variables, never through string interpolation. The app does not use dangerouslySetInnerHTML or any raw HTML injection.

Our app has no backend server and exposes no API endpoints. All state-changing operations are performed through the Monday.com SDK within the iframe, which handles authentication and session management. There are no custom endpoints that could be targeted by CSRF attacks.

In the event of a security breach, we will promptly notify monday.com via their partner communication channels and at security@monday.com. As a client-side only app with no backend or data storage, the attack surface is minimal, but we commit to immediate disclosure if any security issue is identified.

We maintain an automated CI pipeline (GitHub Actions) that runs on every push and pull request. This pipeline includes a mandatory security audit step (npm audit) that flags high-severity vulnerabilities and blocks deployment if any are found. Dependencies are regularly updated and security patches are applied promptly. As a client-side only app with no server infrastructure or database, patching is limited to front-end dependencies, which are kept up to date and redeployed via monday.com's app hosting.

Our app does not store or manage customer data itself. All data segregation is handled by monday.com's infrastructure. Each user accesses the app within their own monday.com iframe session, scoped to their specific board and account. The Monday SDK and GraphQL API enforce access controls, ensuring users can only access data from their own account. There is no shared backend, database, or cache where data from different customers could be mixed.

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer:
The following data is sent to external services:
Customer-submitted data: Board column names, item names, and CSV column headers are sent to AI service(s) for AI-powered column mapping. 
Non-customer-submitted data: Account IDs, board IDs, and user IDs are stored in our database for multi-tenant data management. Error metadata (no PII) is sent for monitoring. Job queue metadata is stored for background processing.
All third-party services are disclosed in the Privacy Policy at taskloops.com/privacy.

Application error logs are stored in Sentry (sentry.io), hosted in the US. Infrastructure logs are stored by Vercel (vercel.com) and Render (render.com) with their default retention policies. No customer PII is included in logs.

Application data is stored in Supabase (PostgreSQL), hosted on AWS in the US. Background job queues are stored in Upstash (Redis), hosted on AWS. Encrypted monday.com access tokens are stored in Supabase using AES-256-GCM encryption. No customer data is stored in local files or browser storage.
Security and privacy inquiries can be directed to hello@taskloops.com

The app is designed with GDPR compliance in mind: (1) Privacy Policy discloses all data collection and third-party services (hosted via Termly at taskloops.com/privacy). (2) Data minimization: only data required for app functionality is collected. (3) Data deletion: when a user uninstalls the app, all associated data is deleted from Supabase. (4) Right of access/deletion: users can request data export or deletion via hello@taskloops.com. (5) No data is sold to third parties.

Customer data access is restricted at multiple levels: (1) Database: Row Level Security (RLS) policies on every table enforce tenant isolation. (2) Infrastructure: Limited access to production systems. (3) Application: The anon key used by the client has RLS restrictions; the service role key is used only in server-side API routes. (4) Third-party services: API keys are scoped to minimum required permissions.

Ripple Import helps teams bring spreadsheet data into monday.com quickly, accurately, and with far less manual work. Import from CSV, XLSX, and multi-sheet Excel files, preview your data before anything is created, map columns to your board, and import into an existing board or into a new board created from the file.

Built for teams working with both simple and structured datasets, Ripple Import supports items, subitems, and multi-level boards. Whether you are importing a flat table, a parent-child structure, or a deeper hierarchy, the app gives you more control over how your data is created inside monday.com. Hierarchy can be detected from a type or level column, a parent reference column, or indentation, and users can also add subitems under an existing item.

Ripple Import includes pre-import validation to help prevent failed imports. Before import starts, the app validates projected board column capacity against monday.com limits:

  • Existing board: current board columns + net new columns required by the selected mapping
  • New board: base board columns + columns created from the file mapping

If the selected setup would exceed monday.com’s board column limit, Ripple Import blocks the import early and tells the user how to adjust mapping (for example, skip or consolidate columns) before continuing.

With Ripple Import, teams can:

  • Import data from CSV and Excel files into monday.com
  • Preview and map columns before import
  • Create missing columns when needed
  • Import into the current board or create a new board from the uploaded file
  • Import items, subitems, and multi-level structures
  • Choose how to handle duplicates
  • Validate rows before import
  • Skip invalid rows and download an issues CSV for review
  • Cancel an import safely and return to the preview step

How to use

  1. Open Ripple Import on your target monday board.
  2. Upload a CSV/XLSX file (or choose a sheet from a multi-sheet workbook).
  3. Choose where to import:
  • into the current board
  • into a new board created from your file
  1. Review and adjust column mapping:
  • map to existing columns,
  • create new columns when needed
  • or skip unnecessary columns.
  1. Configure hierarchy and duplicate-handling settings if needed.
  2. Preview data and run validation checks.
  3. Start import. If there are invalid rows, you can skip them and download an issues CSV for review.

Ripple Import is ideal for teams working with project plans, customer lists, inventory sheets, operational exports, and structured task data that already lives in spreadsheets and needs to be moved into monday.com in a cleaner, more efficient way.

Add the World Map widget to your monday.com dashboard.

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer:
The app sends data to the following destinations:

- Miro (customer-submitted): Item names and field values are sent to Miro's API to populate app cards. This is the core function of the integration. No content data is retained by our application.

- Netlify (non-customer-submitted): The app runs on Netlify, a SOC 2 Type II certified cloud hosting platform. Netlify provides the compute infrastructure but does not store any customer data, all persistent storage is handled exclusively by our encrypted database.

- Axiom (non-customer-submitted): Structured logs containing only user IDs, board IDs, action names, and status codes. No item names or field content. Axiom is SOC 2 Type II certified, hosted on AWS.

- PostHog (non-customer-submitted): Product analytics events containing only user IDs and aggregate counts (e.g., number of cards synced). No item names or field content. PostHog is SOC 2 Type II certified, hosted on AWS.

- Sentry (non-customer-submitted): Error reports and stack traces for debugging purposes only. No customer content is included. Sentry is SOC 2 Type II certified, hosted on GCP.

Structured application logs are sent to Axiom, a SOC 2 Type II certified cloud log management platform hosted on AWS. Logs contain only anonymized identifiers (user IDs, board IDs, action names, status codes) and do not contain customer-submitted content, email addresses, or secrets. PII scrubbing is applied before any data leaves the application server.

App data is stored in a PostgreSQL database provided by Supabase, a SOC 2 Type II certified cloud infrastructure platform hosted on AWS. We store only what is needed to operate the integration: encrypted access tokens and platform-issued IDs. No board content, item names, or user profile data is ever stored. The database is encrypted at rest, and no data is stored locally or in the user's browser.
Security and privacy inquiries can be directed to security@mirosyncformonday.com. We respond to security reports within 48 hours and treat all reported vulnerabilities as high priority.
HIPAA requirements do not apply to MiroSync for monday.com as we do not store or process protected health information (PHI).
The application is not currently SOC 2 or SOC 3 certified. The infrastructure providers (Supabase, Netlify) are SOC 2 Type II certified.

The app stores only what is necessary to provide the sync service: platform-issued user and account IDs, and encrypted access tokens. No email addresses, names, or profile data are stored. Customers can request deletion of their data at any time by revoking the app's access in monday.com, which removes all stored credentials.

All redirects within the application go to pre-approved destinations only: the Miro platform or the app's own URL. No redirect destination is ever derived from user-supplied input, eliminating open redirect vulnerabilities.
All API endpoints only accept and process the specific parameters they expect. Any additional or unexpected parameters in a request are ignored and never passed to the database or internal functions.

We do not log any PII or customer content. Logs contain only the information needed for debugging: action names, resource IDs (board IDs, user IDs), status codes, and durations. Sensitive content is automatically scrubbed before any log data leaves the server.
MFA is enforced on all accounts with access to systems that process customer data. No exceptions.

The app requests only the minimum OAuth scopes needed from Miro and monday.com to perform the sync. Access to production systems is restricted to only those who require it, and exclusively through MFA-protected accounts. No third party has access to customer data.

All user-supplied values are validated and sanitized before use. IDs are restricted to numeric format only, and string values are escaped to prevent injection. The frontend uses React's built-in output encoding and an HTML sanitization library to prevent HTML injection. Input validation is applied consistently across all API endpoints.

The application uses stateless token-based authentication rather than cookies or sessions. Every state-changing API endpoint requires a signed token issued by Miro or monday.com, making cross-site request forgery attacks not applicable. Webhook endpoints additionally use cryptographic signature verification to authenticate incoming requests.

Dependencies are automatically scanned for vulnerabilities on every release. Critical and high severity issues are addressed immediately. Medium and low severity issues are scheduled and resolved on a regular basis. Infrastructure components (hosting, database) are managed by SOC 2 certified providers that handle their own security patching automatically.

Customer data is logically segregated. The app stores only what is needed to operate: encrypted access tokens and card link references. No board content, item names, or user profile data is stored. All records are scoped to a per-user identifier pair extracted from the authenticated session token, never from user-supplied input, so it is not possible for one customer's requests to access another customer's data.

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: The app is hosted entirely on Monday Code, which is covered by monday.com's ISO 27001 certification ([trust.monday.com](https://trust.monday.com)).

The app does not send any data outside of monday.com. There are no external APIs, analytics services, or third-party integrations. All data is stored and processed exclusively within monday.com's platform.
Logs are stored in Monday Code's built-in logging infrastructure, covered by monday.com's SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certifications.

All app data — invoice snapshots, settings, and secrets — is stored exclusively on monday.com's platform via Monday SecureStorage, Storage API, and SecretsManager. No external database or third-party storage is used.

The app runs on Monday Code, which is covered by monday.com's annual third-party penetration testing program. At the application level, we conduct ongoing security audits and automated penetration testing using AI-powered security agents that review the codebase for OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities, authentication weaknesses, and insecure data handling. Application dependencies are continuously scanned via `npm audit` and GitHub Dependabot, and identified issues are remediated before each release.
Security inquiries: security@bam-apps.com. Privacy inquiries: privacy@bam-apps.com.
The app is hosted entirely on Monday Code, which is covered by monday.com's SOC 2 Type II and SOC 3 certifications ([trust.monday.com](https://trust.monday.com)).

The app runs on monday.com's GDPR-compliant platform and stores all data exclusively on Monday infrastructure. All data is purged on uninstall, and the app uses no cookies. Data subject requests can be directed to privacy@bam-apps.com.

The app does not perform any redirects or forwards. There is no OAuth flow — authentication uses monday.com's session token exclusively. No user-supplied URLs are ever used in any redirect, forward, or server-side request.
All API routes explicitly extract and validate individual properties from request bodies. Request bodies are never spread or passed directly to storage.
Logs contain only non-PII identifiers and operation outcomes. Session tokens, email addresses, and user names are never logged.
MFA is enforced on all systems with access to app configuration: GitHub and monday.com Developer Center.

The app requests only the minimum monday.com scopes required for its functionality: `boards:read`, `boards:write`, `me:read`, and `account:read`. No OAuth or third-party API scopes are used. All stored data is scoped to the authenticated account, and only authenticated users within the same account can access or modify data.

The React frontend uses JSX auto-escaping with no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` usage. All user inputs are sanitized both client-side and server-side, and published pages are served with a strict Content Security Policy that blocks all JavaScript execution.
The app uses Bearer token authentication and sets no cookies, so browser-based CSRF attacks cannot forge valid requests.
We maintain an incident response process that includes notifying monday.com within 72 hours of any confirmed breach. Reports can be initiated at security@bam-apps.com.
Monday Code handles all infrastructure-level patching automatically. Application dependencies are monitored via GitHub Dependabot and patched before each release.
Monday Code provides infrastructure isolation between accounts. At the application level, all stored data uses composite keys scoped by account ID, ensuring complete logical isolation.

Delivery Intelligence by IMIRT is the first probabilistic forecasting app on the monday.com marketplace. We use Monte Carlo simulation on your actual monday.com board history to give you probabilistic delivery forecasts. - Probabilistic Forecasting — Four forecast types (How Long, When, How Much, How Likely) powered by your historical completion rates. Colour-coded percentile cards and histogram charts show risk at a glance.

- Risk Buckets — Items automatically classified into Will, May, and At Risk columns based on delivery confidence. Stop guessing which items will land.

- Expected Delivery (xD) — Compare what your team should have delivered against what they actually delivered. Spot drift by week 2, not end of quarter.

- Shot Clock — Time-in-state tracking against your board's historical average, with coaching messages before items stall.

- Find The Reds — Systemic bottleneck detection. Toggle between Acute (items stalled now) and Structural (states that consistently slow everything down).

- Stack The Odds — Dependency-aware delivery intelligence. See which items are blocked, blocking others, or at risk due to upstream dependencies.

- The Work Pitch — Visualise your workflow as a playing field with soccer, GAA, or other sports pitch themes.

- Multi-Board Aggregation — All widgets work across multiple boards for portfolio-level intelligence.


Problems we solve:

- Engineering estimates miss targets by 30-50% — we replace guesswork with probability

- No visibility into which items are actually at risk — we classify risk automatically

- Bottlenecks discovered too late — we detect stalls and structural issues early


Use cases:

- Sprint planning: "Can we realistically finish these 12 items by March 15th?"

- Stakeholder updates: "There's an 85% chance we deliver by the 22nd"

- Continuous improvement: "Items spend 3x longer in Code Review than any other state"

About IMIRT: Built in Newry and Dublin, Ireland by delivery practitioners who use it daily. IMIRT is Irish for "sport" — bringing the discipline of data-driven performance analysis to software delivery. Free for 2 boards.

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: Retainer Pulse is not currently certified under ISO/IEC 27001:2022.

Retainer Pulse does not send customer-submitted board or item data outside monday.com. The app reads connected board data through the monday SDK/API and stores configuration in monday storage. The only backend request is a monday session-token-authenticated storage reset status check; when hosted on monday infrastructure, this remains within monday.com.
Application logs are generated by the app runtime/hosting environment. Retainer Pulse does not implement a separate external log storage service in the application code.

Retainer Pulse stores widget configuration in monday.com instance storage, including selected board IDs, board names, monthly cap, usage column IDs, and optional date column ID. It also stores uninstall reset markers in monday SecureStorage, scoped by account ID.

Security and privacy questions can be sent to 
https://elevixapps.com/support.html
Retainer Pulse is not intended for HIPAA-regulated protected health information and is not currently offered as a HIPAA-compliant application.
Retainer Pulse does not currently have a SOC 2 or SOC 3 report.
Retainer Pulse does not implement arbitrary redirects. The only external navigation opens a monday.com board URL derived from the current monday.com location and the selected board ID.

Retainer Pulse does not expose generic object update endpoints. Backend endpoints accept only limited requests, authenticate them with monday-signed JWTs, and use only expected fields for uninstall reset/status behavior.

The application does not intentionally log secrets, tokens, or customer-submitted board/item content. The code logs operational events and errors only; session tokens and the monday client secret are not logged.

Retainer Pulse requests and uses only the monday.com data needed to provide retainer usage reporting for connected boards. Access is limited by the installing user's monday.com permissions, and the app does not maintain a separate external customer database.
Retainer Pulse sanitizes monday/user-derived text with DOMPurify before displaying or storing relevant values, and the code does not use dangerouslySetInnerHTML.

Retainer Pulse does not use cookie-based authentication for backend state-changing actions. Backend requests are authenticated with monday-signed bearer JWTs, and unauthenticated requests are rejected.
The developer reviews dependency and platform updates, applies security patches as needed, tests changes, and deploys updated frontend/backend code through the monday app deployment tooling.

App configuration is stored in monday instance storage and uninstall reset markers are stored in monday SecureStorage using account-scoped keys. The app does not maintain a shared external customer database.

The app sends and stores limited data outside of monday.com in order to provide its core functionality, including QR automation processing, scan logging, recipe configuration, and authentication handling.

Stored data may include customer-submitted data such as board IDs, item IDs, item names, scan logs, and automation settings.
Sensitive data such as access tokens are encrypted before storage.

Application logs are stored on secured backend infrastructure hosted on DigitalOcean servers.
Logs are used for debugging, monitoring, and security auditing purposes.

Application data is stored in a secured MongoDB database hosted on DigitalOcean Managed MongoDB infrastructure.
Data is encrypted in transit using TLS and sensitive information is encrypted before storage.

Security and privacy related inquiries can be directed to:
support@elasticday.com

We actively monitor and respond to security, privacy, and compliance reports.

The application follows GDPR security and privacy principles, including data minimization, secure storage, encrypted sensitive data, limited data retention, and user data deletion upon uninstall or request.

Customer data is processed only for legitimate application functionality and protected using industry-standard security practices.

The app only allows redirects to approved and trusted domains that are predefined in the application configuration and monday OAuth settings.

User-controlled redirects are not allowed, and all external redirects are validated before execution to prevent open redirect vulnerabilities or malicious destinations.

Database operations never use raw request bodies directly.
All models use controlled field mapping and validation middleware before persistence.

The application is designed to avoid logging sensitive information such as access tokens, secrets, authentication credentials, or personally identifiable information (PII).
Sensitive fields are filtered or masked before logging.
Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is enabled on all critical systems and services used to access or manage customer data, including cloud infrastructure, source control, and administrative accounts.

Access to customer data is restricted based on the principle of least privilege.

The application only requests the minimum OAuth scopes required for functionality, and access to infrastructure, databases, and administrative systems is limited to authorized personnel only.

The application sanitizes and validates all user-supplied input on both the client and server side to protect against Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks.

User input is escaped or sanitized before rendering, and unsafe HTML or script content is not executed.

The backend also validates incoming payloads and rejects malicious or invalid content.

On the frontend, React’s built-in escaping mechanisms are used, and additional sanitization is applied where necessary.

The application protects state-changing operations against CSRF attacks by validating authenticated sessions and request origins.

Sensitive API routes require valid authorization tokens and are protected through backend authentication and request validation mechanisms.

We have internal monitoring and incident response procedures in place.
In the event of a confirmed security incident or data breach affecting monday.com users or services, we will promptly notify monday.com through the appropriate support and security communication channels.

We regularly monitor and update application dependencies, backend services, and infrastructure components to apply security patches and reduce known vulnerabilities.

Security updates are reviewed and deployed as part of our ongoing maintenance process.

Customer data is logically segregated by account and workspace identifiers.
Each customer can only access data associated with their own monday.com account and authorized resources.

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: The app sends no customer data outside monday.com. It runs in the browser and talks only to monday.com's own API and storage; there is no separate server, no analytics, and no third-party tracking. Email content is only ever read into the browser, never sent anywhere else. (The Help link opens our static help page, which collects no data.)

There are no server-side logs; the app runs entirely in the browser with no backend. The only logging is browser-console messages (fixed status text plus monday.com error objects) for diagnostics; nothing is sent to a remote logging service, and no email content, names, addresses, or tokens are logged.
Per-user settings are tagged with the user's monday.com ID; one account-wide entry records which deal an email belongs to (deal IDs, names, and timestamps only, never email content).
Security and privacy questions are answered at support@nichcraft.com, the contact published in our privacy policy and terms of service on nichcraft.com

The app never sends users to a URL it builds from data. Its only built-in link is our own help page opened in a new tab from the Help menu or as a fallback if plan selection fails to open. Email content is cleaned with DOMPurify before display, so any links inside an email are the sender's own and open through the normal browser, not an app redirect.

There is no server-side log store. The app's only logs are browser-console diagnostics (fixed status text and monday.com error objects); no email content, addresses, or secrets are logged. The session token is read client-side (for the view-only gate) but is never logged.

The app asks for read-only access only (boards:read, me:read, updates:read) and never requests write access. boards:read powers the deal-email timeline query and me:read scopes each user's saved filters to their own user ID. Customer data stays in the customer's own monday.com storage, with no standing access on our side.

Everything the app saves to monday.storage is run through DOMPurify in strip mode (all HTML tags and attributes removed) before it is written, across both storage areas. Email HTML is also sanitized with DOMPurify before it is shown.

The app has no server, no cookies, and no cookie-based login, so there is nothing for a CSRF attack to target. Every action runs through the monday.com SDK, authorized by monday.com's session token rather than an automatic cookie.

Dependencies are locked to exact versions via a committed lockfile, and the test suite and linter are run manually before any update is released. Releases are deployed as a draft version and then promoted to live. There is no server or database to patch.

The app has no data store of its own; it saves only to monday.storage, which monday.com keeps separated per account as part of its platform, so one customer's data is never mixed with another's. Within an account, each user's settings are tagged with their monday.com ID.

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: The app is hosted entirely on Monday Code, which is covered by monday.com's ISO/IEC 27001 certification: https://trust.monday.com. Group Card runs on this infrastructure and inherits its controls.

No user data, account data, or workspace data is sent outside of monday.com. Card content, message text, recipient names, user names, board names, item names, account IDs, board IDs, and user IDs all stay within monday.com infrastructure.

The only outbound call the app makes is to a third-party GIF provider (Klipy) to power the optional GIF picker in the signing flow. When a user types into the GIF picker, their search term (e.g. "happy birthday") is sent to Klipy so it can return matching GIFs. The search term is whatever the user freely types into the picker — it does not include any monday data, recipient names, message content, or user/account identifiers.
Logs are stored in Monday Code's built-in logging infrastructure, covered by monday.com's SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certifications.
All app data — card content, settings, OAuth tokens, and secrets — is stored exclusively on monday.com's platform. No external database or third-party storage is used.

We periodically perform penetration testing on Group Card. Our process covers the OWASP Top 10 and OWASP ASVS L1 controls and includes active probes of authentication, authorization (cross-tenant and cross-role), input handling, rate limiting, and outbound egress. A pen test is run before each significant release, and findings are tracked to remediation before the release ships. The most recent pen test (2026-05-28, v1.0.0) returned zero open findings. The hosting platform, Monday Code, is additionally covered by monday.com's own annual third-party penetration testing program.
Security inquiries: security@bam-apps.com. Privacy inquiries: privacy@bam-apps.com.
The app is hosted entirely on Monday Code, which is covered by monday.com's SOC 2 Type II and SOC 3 certifications : https://trust.monday.com

The app runs on monday.com's GDPR-compliant platform and stores all data exclusively on Monday infrastructure. All app data is purged on uninstall, and the app uses no cookies. Data subject requests can be directed to privacy@bam-apps.com.

The only redirect the app performs is to monday.com's own OAuth authorization endpoint. The OAuth state parameter is validated server-side. No user-supplied URLs are ever used in any redirect or forward.
All API endpoints explicitly extract and validate individual fields from request bodies. Request payloads are never spread or passed directly into storage.
Logs contain only non-PII identifiers and operation outcomes. Tokens, email addresses, and user names are never logged.
MFA is enforced on all systems with access to app configuration and source code, including source control and the monday.com Developer Center.

The app requests only the minimum monday.com scopes required for its functionality. Within the app, access to each card is enforced server-side by role (owner, invited signer, recipient, view-only), so users only see and act on what they are entitled to.
User-supplied content is rendered with automatic output encoding and is never injected as HTML. Inputs are validated server-side before storage.
The app authenticates every request with a short-lived bearer token issued by monday.com and sets no cookies, so browser-based CSRF cannot forge valid requests.

monday.com automations stop where the hard parts begin: mirror columns, subitems, multi-level hierarchies, connected boards.


Master Automations is the one app that does all of it. The automations monday.com left out, in a single native app.


In short:

✅ Trigger automations from mirror columns, something monday.com can't do natively

✅ Inherit parent values automatically when subitems are created

✅ Build and automate multi-level subitem hierarchies

✅ Set sequential dependencies across subitems

✅ Sync and roll up values across subitems, parents, and connected boards

✅ Fire dates, moves, and conversions from a single status change

✅ 100% native to monday.com


— What You Can Automate —

Mirror Column Automations: When a mirror column changes, copy its value to a status column on items and subitems.


Subitem Inheritance: When a subitem is created, match its columns to the parent: status, dates, owner, and more. Optionally add the parent name as a prefix.


Multi-Level Hierarchies: Auto-create level 2 and level 3 subitems when an item is created, and set a dropdown to reflect each subitem's depth.


Dependencies: Auto-set the previous subitem as a dependency on creation. When one finishes, the next unlocks. When all are done, the parent updates itself.


Connected Boards Sync: Auto-create and connect linked items across boards on creation, and sync values through connect columns, including subitem-to-subitem across boards.


Status Workflows: One status flip triggers a chain: set a date, move or convert a subitem, clear a connect column, or copy a formula result to a target column.


Rollups: Aggregate subitem values to the parent by sum, count, or most common value. Track progress at the item level and use it in automations.


Sibling Sync: When a subitem column changes, sync the value to all siblings automatically.

Workspace Doctor is a one-click health check for your monday.com account. Built for admins, ops leads, and workspace owners running large or fast-growing accounts, it scans every board for the issues that quietly slow your team down — stale work, status-label drift across boards, items still assigned to people who left, and workspaces no one actually uses.

🩺 What Workspace Doctor scans

📋 Board Health Flags boards no one has updated within your staleness threshold, and boards stuck empty past the grace period.

🏷️ Status Consistency The headline feature. Three-layer detection: fuzzy matching catches typos ("Done"/"done!"), a curated dictionary catches synonyms ("Done"/"Completed"/"Resolved"), and AI embeddings (OpenAI text-embedding-3-small) catch domain-specific terms ("Wrapped Up", "Sealed"). Same-column exclusion prevents false positives.

👤 User Hygiene Detects items still assigned to deactivated users. No more handoffs falling through the cracks when someone leaves.

📊 Adoption Surfaces workspaces with very low recent activity. Abandoned imports, half-started initiatives, ghost departments.

💡 When to use it Run it before a quarterly cleanup, after a reorg or a wave of offboarding, or on a weekly schedule to keep an account tidy as it scales.

🔒 Your data stays in monday Workspace Doctor runs entirely on monday code. Scan results, settings, and OAuth tokens live in your region's Document DB — never on third-party servers. Only short, anonymous status-label strings ("Done", "In Progress") are sent to OpenAI's text-embedding-3-small model for clustering. No item content, board content, or user PII ever leaves monday's infrastructure.

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: For our monday.com integration, the only data related to our customers that is stored in our backend are ID's from monday.com's side. Those ID's are stored on our database where the unique identifier is the Call. Calls are separated from Companies, so no data from one company can be mixed with another.

We run Snyk pipelines in all our repositories and our SRE team is constantly updating our database versions when needed. Also, we have a policy in place with the SLA to fix security issues, which is the following: 
- Critical: 7 days
- High: 30 days
- Medium: 60 days
- Low: Remediation is not mandatory
If a data breach occurs, our security team would reach out to monday.com by email stating the problem and the impact.

For all the state-changing actions, we rely on successfully decoding the JWT signed by Monday APP Client Secret, so we know it's a valid token, we validate that on our end making sure the token is linked to a valid integration and that it's allowed to perform the subsequent actions.

Yes, since we rely on the parameters sent in the body of the request for our Actions handling, the libraries we use to decode JSONs handle that and we don't store any plain text value in our database other than ID's.

Aircall follows a formal process to grant or revoke access to its resources. System access is based on the concepts of "least-possible-privilege" and a "need-to-know" basis to ensure that authorized access is consistent with the defined responsibilities.
We use Okta to access services like AWS and other internal systems. For internal systems that have customer data, a Google Sign-on is required and in order to log into GSuite, Okta is needed.

All of our logs have redactor interceptors which are responsible for redacting out secrets and strings that can be related to PII data from the customer's side. We only keep ID's that help us debug in case of issues.

We don't store data in our databases by directly handling what is sent from the requests. Since we only store information like ID's, we won't store anything extra that an attacker can send to us. We also have validation on the payload in order to validate if we're receiving the correct type of a given field, for example if we expect a number instead of a string, etc.

We don't perform any redirection on our app and we always check that the origin of the request is coming from monday.com. Also we rely on the JWT being valid and correctly signed before doing anything in our integration.

marketplace_app_features.name: GoProof
marketplace_app_features.description:
GoProof's Item View is designed to simplify the process of reviewing and approving files connected to your monday.com item. By integrating with monday.com, GoProof allows you to easily keep track of all your proofs in one place, enabling you to collaborate more effectively with your team.
To create a proof for a file from your monday.com item, simply click on 'Create proof', select the file, add any other necessary details, and click 'Create'. GoProof will then take you to the platform to complete the proof setup process.
Once you've created a proof, a reference to your monday.com item will be automatically added within GoProof. This reference helps maintain a connection between the proof and your monday.com item, making it easy to see up-to-date proof information at a glance.
GoProof's Item View is fully customizable, allowing you to choose what information is most important for you and your team to see. You can select from various options, including the proof's current status, due date, date of approval, and a breakdown of comments left on the proof.

marketplace_app_features.name: Azure DevOps Integration BiSync
marketplace_app_features.description:
Azure DevOps integration app is an easy to use integration between monday and Azure DevOps. Support agents can easily create new Azure DevOps work items and get in touch with developers in one place.

'monday Azure DevOps Integration. They can use this app search and link existing work items and notify Azure DevOps work items. Using this app, you can collaborate with your support team and developers in one place.

monday - Azure DevOps integration app allows the agents to create Azure DevOps work items from monday item easily.

monday - Azure DevOps app also allows syncing of comments and status from Azure DevOps to monday and monday to Azure DevOps. The app integration syncing of comments from monday to Azure DevOps and Azure DevOps to monday will help you alot in increasing the productivity of your team. 'monday Azure DevOps Integration..

monday - Azure DevOps integration app comes with a huge number of Premium features.

The monday Azure DevOps Integration app is totally flexible to meet your needs. If you have any customization requirements. Please contact at support with your requirements and they will help you to meet your requirements! We bring monday - Azure DevOps integration app closer to your business model requirements!

The monday - Azure DevOps app provides huge number of features in the app like Create New Work Item, Link Existing Work Item, Notify linked work items, View History of Work Item, Search Work Item, Customize the view, Configure App and much more.

Create New Work Item:

The Create Work Item: lets the monday user create a new work item # in Azure DevOps platform. The Support agent can select different fields like Project, Work Item Type (like Bug, Feature, Epic,Task, Product Backlog, Issue or any other Custom Work Item), Area, Iteration, Custom Fields, Upload Fields. Based on monday user inputs and selections in the Create new Work Item form, the work item will be created instantly in the Azure DevOps and then display the corresponding information details will be displayed in the Azure DevOps integration app.

-Link Existing Work Item:

The Link button in the monday-Azure DevOps app allows the support agent to link an existing Azure DevOps Workitem # to the current monday item. monday - Azure DevOps app allows the user to create or link multiple work items to one monday item.

-Notify linked Work Items:

Notify button in monday - Azure DevOps app allows the support agent to notify all or particular Azure DevOps work items. The linked item information will be displayed in the comment in the Azure DevOps Work Item. The support agent can also send the files from monday to Azure Devops while notifying.

-Work Item History:

In the monday - Azure DevOps app Work Item history modal shows the details of work item history including the comments and few other details history of the linked work item.

-Configure App:

In the monday-Azure DevOps configure app modal will allow you to map certain fields from monday to Azure DevOps and Azure DevOps to monday.

Search Work Item

The Search button allows the monday agents to search existing work items. 'monday Azure DevOps Integration.. They can link existing work items to any monday items. They can also send the notifications to work items without linking to the current item. They can search the work items based on a couple of parameters directly from Azure DevOps.

Syncing of Comments and Status:

In the monday-Azure DevOps Integration app Syncing lets you enable the syncing of comments,status,attachments from Azure DevOps to monday and syncing of comments from monday to Azure DevOps instantly.

The monday - Azure DevOps Integration app is limited to One Project and upto 20 work items per month in free version.

For more information, please visit our website at https://devopsintegration.io/apps/monday-azure-devops-integration

	•	Analyze Content: Quickly count words, characters and sentences. Estimate reading time to better target your audience.
	•	Transform Text: Instantly convert selected text to UPPERCASE, lowercase, Sentence case, Title Case, or create URL-friendly slugs.

Designed to be intuitive and lightweight, this tool helps you stay focused on creating great content without breaking your workflow. Whether you’re writing reports, planning projects, or collaborating with your team, our app empowers you to polish and manage text inside Workdocs more effectively.

Save time, improve clarity, and make every document shine — all without leaving monday.com!

marketplace_app_features.name: Google Sheets Automations
marketplace_app_features.description:
This is a skill that gets all the rows from a google sheet and returns it to Sidekick.
Sidekick would use the data recieved from the sheet to create a new board.
The Titles of the new board would be the name of the sheet.
The titles of the columns within the new board would be the first row in the spreadsheet.
The type of the columns should be inferred based on the value of each of the columns as well as the header.
This skill can also get information from the users monday board and map it to their google sheet.

marketplace_app_features.name: Get All Spreadsheet rows
marketplace_app_features.description:
Spreadsheet Data Import Action Prompt:
When a user asks any question about importing data from spreadsheets OR mentions Google Sheets accounts/profiles, immediately execute the tool.

Ensure to use the Credentials provided as the token for fetching the available spreadsheets as well as sheet tabs.
Then gather these 2 required pieces of information:

Target Spreadsheet (spreadsheet): The specific spreadsheet document they want to work with - identified by its unique ID from the URL, contains multiple worksheet tabs with data rows.
Target Sheet (sheet): The exact worksheet tab within that spreadsheet where their data is located (e.g., "Sheet1", "Sales Data", "Report").

Use the retrieved combinations to help guide the user in selecting the appropriate account, spreadsheet, and sheet. Do not proceed with any spreadsheet operations until you have confirmed all three elements are properly configured.

If the user provides a spreadsheet link, ask the user what account you should use to access that sheet. When they provide that account, use it with the spreadsheet Id and sheetId to execute this tool.

Use scripting to unlock advanced automations, synchronisation and migrations like a pro.

🧑‍💻 Extend monday.com: go beyond the native functionality of monday.com’s built-in automation engine and implement your most complex business requirements with TypeScript/JavaScript.

🚀 Harness the power of a bespoke solution without any of the hassle: build solutions, not infrastructure. Advanced Automations for monday.com provides you with a fully managed environment, meaning hosting, scaling and security all come built-in. 

🎯 No more workarounds: leave behind performance-sapping mirror column and connected boards automation hacks and implement pro solutions that do exactly what you need - effectively and efficiently.

🦸 Increase productivity by reducing time spent on manual work, developing alternative solutions and context-switching between different apps. 

🤝 Discover a library of scripts, making complex automation a breeze:

Cross-board, workspace and subitem automations

Trigger automations based on advanced logic including boolean and if/else rules, bypass formula column limitations through scripting

Quickly deploy automations with slight variations across your boards

Easy maintenance/updates of your automations without having to start over

Empower a central admin to create automations for everyone so you don’t have to teach and support all your users

 

Please note our app is currently in Beta.

marketplace_app_features.name: Fetch SMS via RingCentral
marketplace_app_features.description:
This block is used to fetch SMS message history and provide it back to the user. In order for this action to be run the following data points are required.
1. Board ID - This can be assumed based on the board that the action is being triggered in
2. Item ID - The item ID should be gathered based on the user defining the target user(s)
3. Phone Column - This should be assumed based on the most populated phone column found on the trigger board. In all cases this should be one of the only values you need to confirm with the user

marketplace_app_features.name: Send SMS via RingCentral
marketplace_app_features.description:
This block is used to send SMS messages to items within the board. In order for this action to be run the following data points are required.
1. Board ID - This can be assumed based on the board that the action is being triggered in
2. Item ID - The item ID should be gathered based on the user defining the target user(s)
3. Phone Column - This should be assumed based on the most populated phone column found on the trigger board. In all cases this should be one of the only values you need to confirm with the user
4. Message - The message is the only other value you need to confirm with the user, this should be gathered by the user providing the message.

marketplace_app_features.name: Same Item Multiple Boards
marketplace_app_features.description:
You are an AI Agent operating within the Same Item Multiple Board (SIMB) app in Monday.com. Your primary responsibility is to help teams keep their workflows aligned across multiple boards by duplicating items when needed. When triggered, you take the origin item (itemId) from the origin board (originBoardId) and create a new item on the target board (targetBoardId) using the same item name. Before duplicating, always verify that the targetBoardId and originBoardId are not the same to avoid redundant copies. If the targetBoardId is not provided, request the user to supply either the board link or board ID of the target board before proceeding. The process may take a short while to complete, so inform the user to wait until the item has been successfully added to the other board.

In addition to duplication, this skill also supports general questions, FAQs, and administrative functions such as usage tracking and checking authorized users.

marketplace_app_features.name: Add Item To Board
marketplace_app_features.description: You are an AI Agent operating within the Same Item Multiple Board (SIMB) app in Monday.com. Your primary responsibility is to help teams keep their workflows aligned across multiple boards by duplicating items when needed. When triggered, take the origin item (itemId) from the origin board (originBoardId) and create a new item on the target board (targetBoardId) using the same item name. Before performing the duplication, always verify that the targetBoardId and originBoardId are not the same to prevent redundant copies. If the targetBoardId is not provided, ask the user to supply either the board link or the board ID of the target board before proceeding. The process may take a short while to add the item to the other board, so please wait until the operation is completed.
